faults.cause: The micro switch did not detect the brewer home position on the required moment.
solution: Check if the brewer is installed correctly. Remove and replace the brewer following the procedure.
Check if the micro leveler is bent.
Check if the motor shaft is broken.
Check if the brewer is blocked and cannot run.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Remove the brewer from the coffee machine and insert it again. Make sure it locks properly. If the problem persists: contact the manufacturer.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.message: Brewer is turning the wrong way, check the wiring
faults.dutch: Brewer is turning the wrong way, check the wiring
faults.cause: Check the wiring in the machine.
solution: Check the wiring of the brewer motor.

faults.message: The brewer blocked during recipe, did not reach position
faults.dutch: The brewer blocked during recipe, did not reach position
faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: • Remove the brewer from the machine and check if the brewer is empty. • Remove any coffee residue from the brewer. • Place the brewer in the coffee machine. In the service menu, select Place brewer in service position and perform a brewer cleaning. Check the section Cleaning the brewer for details.
solution: Open and close the door to initialize the brewer.
Check the operation by taking a coffee.

faults.message: Initialization failed, the brewer did not reach maximum movement
faults.dutch: Initialization failed, the brewer did not reach maximum movement
faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: Take out the brewer and check if the gear can be turned by hand. Check the section Unlock the brewer for details. Place the brewer in the coffee machine and perform a brewer cleaning.
solution: Open and close the door to initialize the brewer.
Check the operation by taking a coffee.

faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: • Check the recipe settings. • Grinder is running too long. • Grinder setting to coarse, resulting in too much ground coffee.
solution: Open and close the door to initialize the brewer.
Check the operation by taking a coffee.

faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: 1. Open and close the door of the coffee machine to initialize the brewer. 2. Check the recipe settings.
solution: Open and close the door to initialize the brewer.
Check the operation by taking a coffee.

faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: 1. Check if a canister must be refilled. See section Fill up the ingredient canisters. 2. Check if the grinder runs to fill the brewer.
solution: Check whether the canister has to be filled. See the section Fill the ingredient canisters.
Check whether the grinder is running and filling the brewer.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.message: Wrong brewer defined in the software
faults.dutch: Wrong brewer defined in the software
faults.cause: Check if the correct configuration is loaded on this coffee machine.
solution: The configuration has to be adjusted.

faults.cause: A too high current is detected on the output for the grinder.
solution: Clean the grinder.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: A too high current is detected on the output of the mixer motor.
solution: Clean the mixing bowl, check the motor.
Check recipes, no dry powder should drop in the mixing bowl.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The dispensed drink did not reach the adjusted amount of water (pulses measured by water flow meter) in time.
solution: If it concerns a drink from the brewer, the filters can be dirty. Run the brewer cleaning cycle with a cleaning tablet to clean the filter.
Check the main water supply, inlet valve.
Check the valve(s).
Check pump(s).
Check if the water flow meter is connected and working correctly.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.message: No water connected / No water in boiler
faults.dutch: No water connected / No water in boiler
faults.cause: No water detected for more than 2 minutes.
solution: First check if the water supply is opened / connected.
Open the door of the coffee machine to display the Service menu, wait 2 seconds and close the door again to allow the coffee machine to re-activate itself.
If this does not help restart the coffee machine (Switch the coffee machine OFF, wait 5 seconds and then switch ON again).
Check inlet valve, pressure reducer and water flow meter.
Check the earth wire connected to the boiler.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The level sensor in the boiler has not detected any water level.
solution: Check whether the tap is open.
Check the level sensor.
Check whether the sensor wiring is connected to the wire harness.
Check the earth connection to the boiler.
Check whether the boiler is losing water because of a leak or a wrongly connected valve.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: • Open and close the machine door for restart, wait until boiler is filled. • If message continues: ▪ Check if main water is connected and available. ▪ Check if inlet valve and pumps works. ▪ Check water system in machine.
solution: Open and close the machine door for a restart. Wait until the boiler is filled.
If the message keeps appearing:
Check whether the water supply is connected and available.
Check whether the inlet valve and pumps are working.
Check the water system in the machine.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The counter has reached the number of cycles.
solution: Install a new filter and reset the counter.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.message: Water filter installed? / Water filter settings not set!
faults.dutch: Water filter installed? / Water filter settings not set!
faults.cause: In service mode the correct selection needs to be made.
solution: Check the section Water filter settings for more details.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Wait until the boiler is heated. If the message is still shown after 10 minutes: check the clixon(s) and heating element.
solution: Wait until the boiler has heated up.
If the message has not disappeared, wait 10 minutes:
check the clixon(s) and the heating element.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Normal start-up message.
solution: Wait until the boiler has heated up.
If the message has not disappeared, wait 10 minutes:
check the clixon(s) and the heating element.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: A temperature of 10 degrees more as the adjusted temperature is detected.
solution: Check if heater is broken and keeps heating.
Check temperature setting.
Check temperature probe.
Check wiring loose/bad contact.
Check that the boilers are connected correctly, don’t switch the wires for boiler one with boiler two.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: A too high resistance is detected on the input of the IO board.
solution: Check if temperature probe is broken, or wiring is loose.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: 1. Clean the drip tray in front of the machine and/or clean the drip bucket inside the waste bucket. 2. Make sure the water level sensors in the drip bucket / drip tray are dry. Also see section Daily maintenance.
solution: Clean the drip tray at the front of the machine and/or clean the brewer's drip tray inside the waste bucket.
Make sure the water level sensors in the drip tray / waste bucket are dry. See the section Daily maintenance.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: External drip tray is not detected.
solution: Place the drip tray.
Check the contacts on the drip tray, clean the contacts on the drip tray and in the machine (they can be dirty or corroded).
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.message: Waste bucket full / Empty waste bucket
faults.dutch: Waste bucket full / Empty waste bucket
faults.cause: Empty waste bucket. • If message is still shown, remove the waste bucket and wait 6 seconds before placing it back. • If message is still shown, check if the waste bucket detector switch is clean. • If a waste bin in a base cabinet is used, reset the waste bin counter or adjust the waste bin full value in Error Settings. • If the problem persists: contact the manufacturer..
solution: Empty the waste bucket.
If the message is still shown, remove the waste bucket and wait 6 seconds before putting it back.
If the message is still shown, check whether the waste bucket detection switch is clean.
If a waste bucket is used in the base cabinet, reset the waste bucket counter or adjust the full waste bucket value in Error settings.
If the problem is not solved: contact the manufacturer.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Check the Message: Waste bucket full / Empty waste bucket for more details.
solution: Clean the waste bucket.
If the message is still shown, check whether the detection switch is clean.
If a waste bucket is used in the base cabinet, reset the waste bucket counter or adjust the empty waste bucket value in Error settings.
faults.note: This message and counter are reset by activating the micro switch behind the waste bucket for at least 3 seconds (remove the waste bucket for at least 3 seconds).
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The micro switch behind the waste bucket does not detect the waste bucket.
solution: Place the waste bucket.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: After a defined number of consumptions the touchscreen needs to be cleaned. Check the section Error settings for more details.
solution: Clean the touchscreen according to the procedure.
faults.note: This function can be switched off in the service menu.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The CoEx® brewer cleaning cycle did not finish correctly or was interrupted.
solution: Run the cleaning cycle again.
faults.note: It is possible to clear this message in the service menu.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The cleaning cycle is required, the time (set in the service menu) has passed.
solution: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: Run the cleaning cycle and the message disappears. The timer is reset.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Perform the following steps to solve the problem: 1. One or more canisters have to be refilled. See the section Fill the ingredient canisters.
solution: One or more canisters have to be refilled. See the section Fill the ingredient canisters.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The cup needs to be placed under the correct dispensing nozzle before the [Order] button is available.
solution: If cup is placed in the correct position, clean the cup sensor.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)
faults.note: The sensitivity of the sensor is adjustable.

faults.cause: The cup needs to be placed under the water dispensing nozzle before the [Order] button is available.
solution: If the cup is placed in the correct position, clean the cup sensor.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

solution: Take the cup or jug away.

faults.cause: Close the door or insert the service key to activate the machine.
solution: Close the door or insert the green service key to activate the machine.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Perform a full payment with coins, tokens or card. Also see section Payment.
solution: Pay the full amount with cash, coins or a card.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The coffee machine is locked during this time by the scheduler and not available for use.
solution: Change the settings in the scheduler.
Check if the clock in the coffee machine is set correctly.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.message: Machine is temporarily out of order
faults.dutch: Machine is temporarily out of order
faults.cause: The message was set on purpose by the operator in the service menu or remotely via ConnectMe. See the chapter Out of order message for more information.
solution: The message was set on purpose by the operator in the service menu or remotely via ConnectMe. See the chapter Out of order message for more information.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: De hoeveelheid pulses voor de waterstroommeter tijdens het opstarten is niet op tijd bereikt.
solution: Open en sluit de machinedeur voor een herstart.
If the message appears again, check the expansion valve, 2 bar valve, pumps, water inlet from the mains and inlet valve.
Check the water flow meter.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: The coffee machine is still busy.
solution: Perform the following steps to solve the problem:

faults.cause: Communication between control board and IO board is not correct.
solution: Check the cable between the boards for damage.
A bad connection on control or IO board can generate this message.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: De configuratie is niet gevonden.
solution: Zie het hoofdstuk Een nieuw configuratiebestand laden vanaf een USB-stick om een configuratie te laden.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Check the section How to load an IPK or FW files from USB to load all files including the user interface.
solution: Zie het hoofdstuk IPK- of FW-bestanden laden vanaf USB om alle bestanden inclusief de gebruikersinterface te laden.
faults.source: TM Avy CoEx Medium NL V1.0 (5DTCET10M)

faults.cause: Check the recipe. • Check if all settings in the recipe are within specifications.
A leak is detected.
solution: Close the water tap.
If open boiler not detected full after 3 minutes of filling: ▪ Check for leaks to or from the open boiler, including drain hose, inlet fill hose above the boiler and outlet valves.
Check ground cable that connects door to cabinet. Ensure that both ends are connected and that the screw on the cabinet connector is tight.
Inspect open boiler level sensor (wiring/connector, scale buildup/corrosion).
Replace open boiler level sensor.
Check inlet water supply and/or external filters.

TM Nio CoEx XL EN V1.1.1 (5DTXKA20M)

components.title: Function of the components
components.text: In the next paragraphs you find a detailed description of the several parts and components in the machine. Understanding of the function of the different components is essential for maintaining the machines.

components.title: Hot water system (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The water system is positioned at the back side of the machine and accessible from the back. If water and power are connected and the door is closed the water system starts filling the boiler(s) automatically. The water system consists of the following main components:
Back inside view CoEx (Medium model)
METAL valves (left)
PPSU valves (right)
1. Open boiler
2. Pressure valves (CoEx)
- METAL (left picture)
- PPSU (right picture)
3. Water flow meter
4. Inlet valve
5. Pressure reducer
6. Water pumps
7. Pressure boiler
8. Outlet valves open boiler

components.title: Inlet valve (CEC, XEA)
components.text:
The double inlet valve is controlled by the level sensors in the boilers and is switched on during a dispense of hot water to the brewer or mixer. One valve is used for the pressure boiler, the second one for the open boiler.
The inlet valves are 24V DC valves. The inlet valves contain a backflow protection. This backflow protection is preventing that water is flowing back into the water supply.
Electrical connections / wire colors
Function
Wiring color
Common (+24V)
Orange
Output (0) valve 1 - open boiler
Red / Green
Output (0) valve 2 - pressure boiler
Orange / Green

components.title: Inlet valve (CND, FEC, FND)
components.text:
The inlet valve is controlled by the level sensor in the boiler and is switched on during a dispense of hot water to the brewer or mixer. The inlet valve is a 24V DC valve. The inlet valve contains a backflow protection. This backflow protection is preventing that water is flowing back into the water supply.
• 24 VDC
• Coil: 9.4 Watt, 60Ω
• Black flow restrictor in outlet, 2.7 liter/min.
• With backflow protection

components.title: Boiler (Filterfresh Medium / Filterfresh Small)
components.text:
The water system is positioned at the back side of the machine and is accessible from the back. If water and power are connected and the door is closed, the water system starts filling the boiler(s) automatically.
The Uni-brewer model contains one open boiler that provides hot water for the Uni-brewer, the mixers, the optional tea brewer, and the hot water outlet.

components.title: Boiler (Instant Medium)
components.text:
The water system is positioned at the back side of the machine and is accessible from the back. If water and power are connected and the door is closed, the water system starts filling the boiler(s) automatically.
The Instant medium model contains one open boiler that provides hot water for the mixers and the hot water outlet.

components.title: Boiler (Instant Small)
components.text:
The water system is positioned at the back side of the machine and is accessible from the back. If water and power are connected and the door is closed, the water system starts filling the boiler(s) automatically.
The Instant small model contains one open boiler that provides hot water for the mixers, the optional tea brewer, and the hot water outlet.

components.title: Pressure reducer (CoEx Medium / CoEx Small)
components.text:
The pressure reducer reduces the water pressure to a stable pressure independent from the inlet pressure from the mains water supply. The required inlet pressure from the water supply is between 1,0 and 6 bar. The pressure reducer is adjusted to an outlet pressure of about 0,8 - 0,9 bar during an espresso cycle.
The input and output hose to the reducer must be connected in the right direction, the reducer works incorrectly in the reversed mode. There is an arrow on the side of the reducer indicating the correct water flow direction. The reducer contains a backflow protection. This backflow protection prevents the possibility that water from the machine is flowing back into the main water supply.
Procedure to adjust the pressure
Perform the following steps:
1. Remove the lower plate from the back of the machine.
2. Remove the plug P1 (see inset). ▪ Check the Hot water system (on page 27) inside view for more details.
3. Connect the manometer to the hose.
4. Pull out the knob to unlock the reducer.
5. Select an (double) espresso.
6. Adjust the reducer by turning the knob during the pump cycle of the espresso selection.
▪ The manometer must show 0,8 - 0,9 bar during an espresso cycle.
▪ Turning clockwise => increase output pressure (when seen from above)
▪ Turning counter clockwise => decrease output pressure
7. Lock the reducer by pushing the knob downwards.
8. Disconnect the manometer and insert the plug in the hose.
9. Place the back plate on the machine.
10. Ready.

Temperature sensor
The temperature is adjustable in the service menu. The optimal temperature setting is 91 ºC.
The control system contains several safeties and will display warning messages based on the detected value of the temperature sensor:
• A too high temperature, too low temperature, shortcut or disconnected sensor
• Disconnected temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is above 350 kW.

Level sensor
The level in the boiler is detected by the stainless steel housing of the level sensor. The boiler is connected to ground. On the sensor housing a positive signal is applied from the control system. If the water level reaches the sensor, a current will to pass through the water and the control system will detect this.

components.title: Water flow meter
components.text:
The water flow meter (water counter) measures the quantity of the water flowing through the water system.
Three functions are based on the water flow meter:
1. The water dosages for the consumptions are based on quantity of the pulses generated by the flow meter.
2. During the startup procedure it is detected if water is flowing into the system. If not, the machine will stop working and show the error messages “start-up problem” and “no water connected”
3. The amount of heating of the boiler is, besides the measurement with the temperature probe, also based on the quantity of incoming water.
The water flow meter is built in between the pressure reducer and the pumps.
It is a small turbine which produces electrical pulses. Each 360º rotation produces 2 pulses in the sensor (Hall element). The pulses are detected by the control system. The hose to the water flow meter must be connected in the correct position; the flow meter cannot detect water in the reverse mode. There is a small arrow on the water flow meter which shows the right direction.
The water flow meter is a 1.8 mm type. Each pulse is about 0.8 ml water.

components.title: Temperature safety (FEC, FND, IEA)
components.text:
Temperature safety / clixon
The temperature safety (also known as clixon) protects the heater against overheating if the control system does not switch off the heater. The safety interrupts the current to the heater directly, if the boiler is overheating. The safety is a housing with a bi-metal disc. If the device gets too hot, the bi-metal disc opens a (normally closed contact) switch.
Internals of the Temperature safety
1. Switching arm
2. Transfer pin
3. Base
4. Disc retainer
5. Cap
6. Bi-metal Disc
After cooling down, the safety switch can be reset by pressing the pin (1) by hand.
Temperature Safety values
This coffee machine contains one open boiler:
The open boiler contains two different clixons.
• A boil dry safety, positioned on the top lid of the open boiler. This clixon switches off when the temperature is over 110 °C ± 5 °C.
• A temperature safety, positioned in the overflow hose of the open boiler. This clixon switches off when the temperature of the overflow water is over 90 °C ± 5 °C.

components.title: Water pump
components.text:
The pumps are generating the pressure and flow of the water. The pumps increase the pressure to the required brewing pressure (between 1.5 and 10 bar). The pump is a vibration pump. The plunger vibrates up and down to build up pressure.
The pump is a 24VAC pump, the electrical signal to the pump is a 24V block pulse. The pressure can be adjusted by the electrical signal (pulse-width) to the pump. A longer pulse gives a higher pressure because the plunger is lifted higher. The maximum pulse width is 20. This figure can be set in the service program, individual for every consumption. Because of the high frequency of the pulses this electronic signal cannot be measured with an ordinary volt meter. The pulses for the two pumps run out of phase, so a stable high pressure is offered to brew an espresso.
P1 — Pump 1
P2 — Pump 2
PW — Pulse width

Thermal protection
The pump is protected with a self resettable thermal cutout, acting as a safety. If the pump runs for more then 15 minutes continuously without water, this thermal cutout gets too hot and switches the power to the pump off. When the pump and the thermal cutout are cooled down again, the thermal cutout switches on automatically.

components.title: Boiler (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The water system is positioned at the back side of the machine and is accessible from the back. If water and power are connected and the door is closed, the water system starts filling the boiler(s) automatically.

The 2-way outlet valves are used for the hot water to the Uni-brewer, hot water to the mixers and the hot water outlet.
When a drink is selected on the operating panel, the control system sends a signal to one of the outlet valves to open for a set time. This time (the dosed water quantity) can be set in the control system of the machine. When the setting for the water quantity is enhanced, the outlet valve (1) is opened for a longer period, and the dosed water quantity will be increased.
Depending on the selected choice, the water will be dosed into the mixer or directly into the cup. The dosing speed of the outlet valve can be adjusted on the outlet valve itself with the screw. As a result of this, it is possible to dose more ingredients at the same dosed water quantity. This is particularly applicable to dissolve instant ingredients. The valves are default adjusted on an open hole of 2 mm/0.0787 in.

Temperature sensor
The temperature is adjustable in the service menu (Boiler temperature (see Boiler(s) on page 120)). The optimal temperature setting of the pressure boiler is 92 ºC. If no consumptions are made, the temperature in the boiler will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer.
The control system contains safeties and the warning messages are based on the detected value of the temperature sensor:
• A too high temperature, too low temperature, shortcut or disconnected sensor is detected by the control system.
• Disconnected temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is above 350 kW.
• Shortcut temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is below 1 kW.
• Unlikely temperature measured, replace temperature sensor(s).
Level sensor
The water level in the boiler is detected by the temperature/level sensor. The boiler is connected to ground. On the isolated sensor housing a positive signal is applied from the control system. If the water level reaches the sensor, a current will pass through the water to the ground and the control system will detect this.

The temperature is adjustable in the service menu (Boiler temperature (see Boiler(s) on page 118)). The optimal temperature setting of the pressure boilers is 80 ºC in boiler 1 and 92 ºC in boiler 2. If no consumptions are made, the temperature in boiler 2 will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer.
The control system contains safeties and the warning messages are based on the detected value of the temperature sensor:
• A too high temperature, too low temperature, shortcut or disconnected sensor is detected by the control system.
• Disconnected temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is above 350 kW.
• Shortcut temp. sensor is generated if the resistance is below 1 kW.
• Unlikely temperature measured, replace temperature sensor(s).
Level sensor
The water level in the boiler is detected by the temperature/level sensor. The boiler is connected to ground. On the isolated sensor housing a positive signal is applied from the control system. If the water level reaches the sensor, a current will pass through the water to the ground and the control system will detect this.

components.title: 2-way outlet valve (Open boiler)
components.text:
The 2-way valve is the outlet from the hot water system to a component. The valves are stacked and connected to the boiler.
The normally closed (NC) valve is controlled by 24VDC from the IO-board. When a drink is selected, the control system sends a signal to one of the outlet valves to open for a set time. This time (the dosed water quantity) is set in the control system of the machine. The dosing amount of the outlet valve can be adjusted on the outlet valve itself (calibrated). As a result of this, it is possible to dose more ingredients at the same dosed water quantity. This is particularly applicable to dissolve instant ingredients.
Calibrate the valve (when not installed)
The valves are factory set to open 1.5 mm.
To set a new valve to 1.5 mm before installation: insert a 1.5 mm Hex wrench as a measuring device into the valve outlet and use a 5 mm Hex wrench to close the nozzle until it 'grips' the 1.5 mm wrench. Install the valve.
Calibrate the valve (when installed)
To calibrate an open boiler valve inside the coffee machine, follow these steps:
1. Open the door.
2. Remove the canisters.
3. Remove the cover behind the canisters by removing two screws.
4. Login to the Service Menu
5. Select in the menu: Hardware > Calibrations.
6. Place a measuring cup on the cup stand.
7. Test the correct valve (check the picture in 'Positioning of the valves' to see which valve).
8. Tap the [Calibrate] button of the desired valve.
9. The correct amount is 125 ml (in 7 seconds).
10. Adjust the setting of the valve. ▪ Turn counterclockwise for more water (see inset)
▪ Turn clockwise for less water
11. Test 3 times, add the results and divide by 3. A result between 122.5 ml and 127.5 ml is OK.
12. Ready.

components.title: Temperature safety (CND, XNA)
components.text:
Temperature safety / clixon
The temperature safety (also known as clixon) protects the heater against overheating if the control system does not switch off the heater. The safety interrupts the current to the heater directly, if the boiler is overheating. The safety is a housing with a bi-metal disc. If the device gets too hot, the bi-metal disc opens a (normally closed contact) switch.
Internals of the Temperature safety
1. Switching arm
2. Transfer pin
3. Base
4. Disc retainer
5. Cap
6. Bi-metal Disc
After cooling down, the safety switch can be reset by pressing the pin (1) by hand.
Temperature Safety values
This coffee machine contains two pressure boilers:
The pressure boiler contains two identical clixons.
• They are both positioned on the side of the pressure boiler. They switch off when the temperature is over 110 °C ± 5 °C.

components.title: Filterfresh brewing system
components.text:
Brewer chamber
2. Transport wheels
3. Brewer outlet
4. Piston
5. Cylinder
The brewer works on the vacuum principle.
Ground coffee is dosed into the brewer chamber together with the hot water. At that moment the brewer is at rest (A). Then the brewer motor turns and the piston moves up (B). That movement mixes the water and the coffee, which improves extraction. So less ground coffee is needed for a stronger, more flavourful coffee. The piston then moves down, pulling the coffee through the filter paper (C). The coffee flows out of the cylinder through the outlet into the cup. The filter paper, together with the coffee residue, is carried off by the transport wheels once the piston is almost at its lowest position and the brewer chamber is up. After this the brewer returns to rest (D) and the next cycle can start.

components.title: Removing the brewer
components.text:
Required
Use the following items for the procedure:
• Blue brewer key
• Green service key
Procedure
Do the following:
1. Tear off the filter paper to the left and right of the brewer.
2. Put the service key in the door.
3. In the service menu tap [Maintenance] and then [Replace filter paper].
▪The brewer chamber moves to the open position.
4. Take the service key out of the door.
5. Remove the brewer chamber by pulling it in the direction of the arrow.
6. Remove the rest of the old filter paper from the brewer. ▪Lift the transport wheels with the lever if needed.
7. Take the nozzle/outlet off the brewer.
8. Take the brewer out of the machine. Tilt the lower part of the brewer towards you to free the shaft from the motor interlock.
▪Tilting the lower part about 10
cm is enough.
9. Lift the brewer slightly so the lugs come out of the suspension, and take the brewer out of the coffee machine.

components.title: Fitting the brewer
components.text:
Before you refit the brewer, check that the brewer chamber is in the open position.
▪If needed, position the shaft so it fits the
motor interlock.
2. Put the lugs at the back of the brewer into the two suspension holes.
3. Lower the brewer and make sure the shaft seats in the motor interlock.
▪Some force is needed to lock the brewer
properly.
4. Fit the nozzle/outlet onto the brewer.
5. Guide the filter paper through the brewer. Lift the transport wheels with the lever if needed.
▪More information is in the section Replacing the filter
paper.
6. Fit the brewer chamber. Push the brewer chamber with the two pins into position.
7. Put the service key in the door.
8. In the service menu tap [Maintenance] and then [Replace filter paper] so the brewer runs a cycle.
▪Check that the filter paper is transported properly and
evenly.

components.title: Clamp force setting
components.text:
The clamp force has to be readjusted if too much water leaks between the brewer and the brewer chamber. That is the case when the filter paper gets wet over more than 10 mm all round the brewer chamber. If the clamp force is set too high, however, excessive wear can occur or the brewer motor can jam.
Adjust the clamp force of the brewer chamber as follows:
1. Open the machine door.
2. Tear off the filter paper in front of and behind the brewer.
3. Take the brewer out of the machine.
4. Turn the brewer piston up with the Uni key until the brewer chamber tilts.
5. Remove the filter paper from the brewer. Put a new piece of filter paper between the brewer and the brewer chamber.
6. Put the brewer piston in the top position (connecting rods in line).
7. Turn the adjusting nut on top of the H frame clockwise until the filter paper is just clamped between the brewer and the brewer chamber. The brewer chamber must not be pushed onto the brewer while adjusting.
8. Turn the nut ½ – 1 turn clockwise.
9. Put the brewer in the machine.
10. Fit the filter paper following the procedure described in the user manual.
11. Check the brewer works by selecting a coffee drink.
12. Close the machine door.

components.title: Paper transport distance
components.text:
To prevent old coffee from remaining in the brewer chamber, the distance between the layers of coffee residue can be adjusted while the filter paper is transported. This may be needed especially with large coffee dosing quantities. To avoid unnecessary loss of paper (replacing the paper reel more often), however, the distance between the layers should not be set too large.
Adjusting the clamping force affects the paper transport.
The paper transport is adjusted correctly when: no coffee residue remains in the brewer chamber after the filter paper has been transported; the distance between the layers of coffee residue is between 5 and 10 mm.
Adjust the paper transport as follows:
1. Hold the adjustment bolt and loosen the lock nut.
2. Turn the adjustment bolt to the left if coffee residue remains in the brewer chamber / turn the adjustment bolt to the right if the distance between the layers of coffee residue is too large.
3. Tighten the lock nut.
4. Check the operation of the paper transport.
5. Check the distance between the layers of coffee residue.
6. Place the service key in the door switch. The machine is now switched on.
7. Take at least 4 consumptions to test the transport distance of the paper.
8. Check that the machine works properly by taking a test drink (coffee). Place the cup or rinsing bowl under the outlet to collect the hot test drink.

components.title: Removing the brewer chamber
components.text:
The brewer chamber has to be taken out weekly for cleaning. With the brewer in the open position the chamber can be removed.
When putting the brewer chamber back, make sure the pins seat properly.

components.title: 2-way outlet valve (Open boiler) — CoEx XL Medium
components.text:

This time (the dosed water quantity) is set in the control system of the machine. The dosing amount of the outlet valve can be adjusted on the outlet valve itself (calibrated). As a result of this, it is possible to dose more ingredients at the same dosed water quantity. This is particularly applicable to dissolve instant ingredients.
Calibrate the valve (when not installed)
The valves are factory set to open 1.5 mm.
To set a new valve to 1.5 mm before installation: insert a 1.5 mm Hex wrench as a measuring device into the valve outlet and use a 5 mm Hex wrench to close the nozzle until it 'grips' the 1.5 mm wrench. Install the valve.
Calibrate the valve (when installed)
To calibrate an open boiler valve inside the coffee machine, follow these steps:
1. Open the door.
2. Remove the canisters.
3. Remove the cover behind the canisters by removing two screws.
4. Login to the Service Menu
5. Select in the menu: Hardware > Calibrations.
6. Place a measuring cup on the cup stand.
7. Check the correct valve (check the picture in 'Positioning of the valves' to see which valve).
8. Tap the [Calibrate] button of the desired valve.
9. The correct amount is 125 ml (in 7 seconds).
10. Adjust the setting of the valve. ▪ Turn counterclockwise for more water (see inset)
▪ Turn clockwise for less water
11. Test 3 times, add the results and divide by 3. A result between 122.5 ml and 127.5 ml is OK.
12. Ready.

components.title: Brewer cycle (CoEx XL) — CoEx XL Small
components.text:
The CoEx XL brewer cycle
This is one complete cycle of the CoEx XL brewer.
1. The CoEx XL brewer is in the starting position. The brewer cylinder is clamped against the coffee filter so that a brewer chamber is formed. The grinder runs and the ground coffee falls from the grinder outlet into the brewer chamber (1).
2. Two motor-driven transport lead screws (1) move the piston (2) back and forth. During grinding, coffee that falls into the brewer chamber is pushed towards the end to prevent spillage. This can be useful when a double dosage of ground coffee is selected.
3. Once the required dosage is reached, grinding stops. The piston (1), with the inlet filter (2) on top, moves inside the cylinder. The ground coffee is pressed against the rotating coffee filter (3), creating a coffee puck (CP).
4. Hot water enters the brewer via a small hose (1) connected to the inlet filter and is pressed through the coffee puck (CP), the coffee filter (2) and into the flow regulator (3).
5. The needle (4) in the flow regulator moves to regulate the flow (pressure and extraction time).
6. At the end of the brewing cycle the needle moves to the ‘aerate’ position so the coffee outlet can empty.
7. The piston (1) moves backwards and connects to the brewer cylinder by means of the clutches (2) and (3) and pulls the brewer cylinder away from the coffee filter.
8. The piston (1) moves forward again, disconnects all clutches and leaves the brewer cylinder in the same position. The used coffee puck is pressed out of the cylinder.
The coffee puck wiper (2) moves the coffee to the waste bucket and removes coffee residue from the surface of the inlet filter.
9. The piston (1) moves fully forward and presses the brewer cylinder (2) against the coffee filter (3), where it stays locked.
10. The needle (4) moves to the “flush” position to lead any remaining output to the drain outlet.
11. The piston returns to the starting position and is ready for the next dispense.
12. The needle in the flow regulator returns to the starting position.

components.title: Removing and fitting the CoEx XL brewer (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
Removal procedure
To remove the brewer, do the following:
1. To take the brewer out of the coffee machine, put four fingers in the lower grip (1). Push the catch (2) in with your thumb and pull the brewer out of the frame (3) in the direction of the arrow.
Fitting procedure
To fit the brewer, do the following:
1. Make sure the inside of the brewer frame is clean.
2. Put the brewer in the frame and push it into the catches.
▪All other couplings are made automatically.
▪The brewer initialises once when the first coffee dispense is started. All brewer parts are first moved to the correct starting position.

components.title: Replace service parts in the brewer (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
The only parts in the brewer that have to be replaced after 50,000 brewing cycles (or after 2 years) are:
1. the coffee filter with seals
2. the inner cylinder
3. the inlet filter with seals.
A complete set of spare parts is available.
The CoEx XL serial number (visible on a heat- and water-resistant label on the brewer gear box) contains the production date. The number format is year-week-sequence number.
Procedure
Follow the steps to replace the service parts.
1. Before you remove the brewer from the machine, first place it in the Service position. There is an option in the service menu that can help you with this. See the chapter Place brewer in service position (on page 60).
2. Remove the brewer from the machine and take the cover off the brewer. For more information, see the chapter ‘Remove and clean the brewer’ in the user manual.
Remove inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove the one screw (1) that fixes the inlet filter. (M4/Length=16mm)
2. Turn the inlet filter to the right (2) to open the bayonet catch.
3. Release the inlet filter and take it off the piston.
Remove inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove 1 screw that fixes the inner cylinder. (M4/Length=16mm).
2. Turn the brewer around again.
3. Slide the inner cylinder (1) out of the outer cylinder. Tilt (2) it and remove it from the brewer.
Replace coffee filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Push the cylinder down by hand.
2. If the cylinder is locked, find the clutches on the left (L) and right (R) side. Push the right clutch up (or push from the back) and at the same time push the left clutch down. The cylinder can now move freely. Move it down to reach the coffee filter.
3. Place the brewer in vertical position, with the brewer locking facing up.
4. Locate the 2 screws between the gears. Loosen the 2 screws and remove them. (3.5/Length=8mm)
5. Remove the old coffee filter.
6. Fit the new coffee filter. ▪Make sure the (coffee) water connections are in line
with each other.
▪If needed, turn the coffee filter slightly so that the square
filter holder fits into the drive gear.
7. Fix the coffee filter with 2 screws.
Install inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Place the brewer on a flat surface as shown in the picture. Push the cylinder against the coffee filter.
2. Put the inner cylinder in the brewer and tilt it around the piston.
3. Slide it into the outer cylinder.
4. Turn the brewer upside down. Fix the inner cylinder with 1 screw (M4x16).
Install the inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Fit the new inlet filter. ▪Align it with the transparent water coupling (inset 1).
▪Lower the filter onto the bayonet catch (inset 2) and
turn the filter to lock it.
▪Fix the inlet filter with 1 screw (3). (M4/
Length=16mm)
2. Done! The service parts are installed.
3. Fit the cover and install the brewer in the coffee machine.

components.title: Unlocking the brewer (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
In rare cases the brewer system can lock itself. If, for instance, the door of the coffee machine is opened during a coffee cycle, the brewer is stopped for safety and can stay in an unknown position.
1. Take the brewer out of the coffee machine.
2. Take off the cover.
3. Turn the gear (1) and check whether the piston moves up and down on the two lead screws (see arrows).
4. Fit the brewer in the coffee machine and draw a coffee.

components.title: Putting the brewer in the service position (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter first has to be pulled out of the coffee chamber. The service menu has an option that helps with this. See the chapter Service position CoEx XL (on page 122) for more information.
If that option is not available in the service menu, it has to be done by hand.
1. Open the door and take the brewer out of the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) anticlockwise.
4. The piston with the inlet filter moves to the lowest position.

components.title: Removing and fitting the CoEx XL brewer (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
Removal procedure
To remove the brewer, do the following:
1. To take the brewer out of the coffee machine, put four fingers in the lower grip (1). Push the catch (2) in with your thumb and pull the brewer out of the frame (3) in the direction of the arrow.
Fitting procedure
To fit the brewer, do the following:
1. Make sure the inside of the brewer frame is clean.
2. Put the brewer in the frame and push it into the catches.
▪All other couplings are made automatically.
▪The brewer initialises once when the first coffee dispense is started. All brewer parts are first moved to the correct starting position.

components.title: Replace service parts in the brewer (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
The only parts in the brewer that have to be replaced after 50,000 brewing cycles (or after 2 years) are:
1. the coffee filter with seals
2. the inner cylinder
3. the inlet filter with seals.
A complete set of spare parts is available.
The CoEx XL serial number (visible on a heat- and water-resistant label on the brewer gear box) contains the production date. The number format is year-week-sequence number.
Procedure
Follow the steps to replace the service parts.
1. Before you remove the brewer from the machine, first place it in the Service position. There is an option in the service menu that can help you with this. See the chapter Place brewer in service position (on page 67).
2. Remove the brewer from the machine and take the cover off the brewer. For more information, see the chapter ‘Remove and clean the brewer’ in the user manual.
Remove inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove the one screw (1) that fixes the inlet filter. (M4/Length=16mm)
2. Turn the inlet filter to the right (2) to open the bayonet catch.
3. Release the inlet filter and take it off the piston.
Remove inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove 1 screw that fixes the inner cylinder. (M4/Length=16mm).
2. Turn the brewer around again.
3. Slide the inner cylinder (1) out of the outer cylinder. Tilt (2) it and remove it from the brewer.
Replace coffee filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Push the cylinder down by hand.
2. If the cylinder is locked, find the clutches on the left (L) and right (R) side. Push the right clutch up (or push from the back) and at the same time push the left clutch down. The cylinder can now move freely. Move it down to reach the coffee filter.
3. Place the brewer in vertical position, with the brewer locking facing up.
4. Locate the 2 screws between the gears. Loosen the 2 screws and remove them. (3.5/Length=8mm)
5. Remove the old coffee filter.
6. Fit the new coffee filter. ▪Make sure the (coffee) water connections are in line
with each other.
▪If needed, turn the coffee filter slightly so that the square
filter holder fits into the drive gear.
7. Fix the coffee filter with 2 screws.
Install inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Place the brewer on a flat surface as shown in the picture. Push the cylinder against the coffee filter.
2. Put the inner cylinder in the brewer and tilt it around the piston.
3. Slide it into the outer cylinder.
4. Turn the brewer upside down. Fix the inner cylinder with 1 screw (M4x16).
Install the inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Fit the new inlet filter. ▪Align it with the transparent water coupling (inset 1).
▪Lower the filter onto the bayonet catch (inset 2) and
turn the filter to lock it.
▪Fix the inlet filter with 1 screw (3). (M4/
Length=16mm)
2. Done! The service parts are installed.
3. Fit the cover and install the brewer in the coffee machine.

components.title: Unlocking the brewer (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
In rare cases the brewer system can lock itself. If, for instance, the door of the coffee machine is opened during a coffee cycle, the brewer is stopped for safety and can stay in an unknown position.
1. Take the brewer out of the coffee machine.
2. Take off the cover.
3. Turn the gear (1) and check whether the piston moves up and down on the two lead screws (see arrows).
4. Fit the brewer in the coffee machine and draw a coffee.

components.title: Putting the brewer in the service position (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter first has to be pulled out of the coffee chamber. The service menu has an option that helps with this. See the chapter Service position CoEx XL (on page 130) for more information.
If that option is not available in the service menu, it has to be done by hand.
1. Open the door and take the brewer out of the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) anticlockwise.
4. The piston with the inlet filter moves to the lowest position.

components.title: Calibrating the brewer / water flow meter (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the amount of water and is calibrated at the factory. When the flow meter is replaced it has to be calibrated once. The system has to ‘know’ how much water enters the brewer and where the needle in the flow regulator must sit so the amount of water is right. See the procedure in the chapter Calibrations (on page 105) for more information.

components.title: Mixer (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
The mixer consists of a mixer motor, a mixer propeller and a mixer housing. The mixer is controlled by the control board and ensures the ingredient(s) and water mix properly. The rotating propeller mixes air through the water and the ingredients, forming a layer of foam. That improves the taste and the look of the drink.
Motor specification: 24VDC, 14,000 rpm. In the event of a blockage a safeguard on the IO board is tripped and the message “mixer blocked” appears on the screen.
A restricted inlet diameter of the mixer housing gives a good flow in the mixing bowl.

components.title: Filterfresh brewing system
components.text:
Brewer chamber
2. Transport wheels
3. Brewer outlet
4. Piston
5. Cylinder
The brewer operates according to the vacuum principle.
Ground coffee is dosed into the brewer chamber, together with the hot water. At that moment the brewer is in the rest mode (A).
Then the brewer motor turns, moving the piston up (B). This movement mixes the water and the coffee mixed, improving the extraction. Consequently, less ground coffee is necessary to obtain stronger and more tasteful coffee. Subsequently, the piston moves down, pulling the coffee through the filter paper (C). The coffee flows out of the cylinder through the outlet into the cup. The filter paper together with the coffee residue is transported by means of the transport wheels, when the piston is in the almost lower position and the brewer chamber is lifted.
After this, the brewer returns to the rest mode (D) and is ready for the next cycle.

components.title: Brewer cycle (CoEx XL)
components.text:
The CoEx XL brewer cycle
This is one complete cycle of the CoEx XL brewer.
1. The CoEx XL brewer is in starting position. The brewer cylinder is locked against the coffee filter to create a brewer chamber.
The grinder runs and the ground coffee falls from the grinder outlet into the brewer chamber (1).
2. Two, motor powered, transport lead screws (1) move the piston (2) back and forth. During grinding, coffee dropped in the brewer chamber is pushed towards the end to prevent spillage. This can be useful when a double dosage of ground coffee is selected.
3. When the required dosage is reached, grinding stops. The piston (1), with on top the inlet filter (2) moves inside the cylinder. The ground coffee, is pressed against the rotating coffee filter (3) creating a coffee puck (CP).
4. Hot water is inserted in the brewer cylinder via a small hose (1) connected to the inlet filter and pressed through the coffee puck (CP), through the coffee filter (2) and into the flow regulator (3).
5. The needle (4) inside the flow regulator moves to regulate the flow (pressure and extraction time).
6. At the end of the brewing cycle, the needle is moved to the ‘aerate’ position to allow the coffee outlet to empty.
7. The piston (1) moves back and connects to the brewer cylinder using the clutches (2) and (3) and pulls the brewer cylinder away from the coffee filter.
8. The piston (1) moves forward again, disconnects all clutches and leaves the brewer cylinder in the same position. The used coffee puck is pushed out of the cylinder. The coffee puck wiper (2) moves the coffee to the waste bucket and cleans the surface of the inlet filter from coffee residue.
9. The piston (1) moves forward completely and pushes the brewing cylinder (2) against the coffee filter (3) where it remains locked.
10. The needle (4) moves to the ‘flush’ position to redirect any remaining output to the drain outlet.
11. The piston returns to the start position and is ready for the next brew.
12. The needle in the flow regulator returns to the starting position.

components.title: Brewer cycle
components.text:
Home position / Start position.
After dosing the coffee the brewer start running. The motor runs clockwise till closed position.
Closed position
The dosed coffee is pressed together between the upper and lower piston. After pressing the coffee together the water is dosed through the piston, into the coffee cake and flows through the filter screen out into the top and outlet of the brewer. The pressure from the piston on the coffee cake is regulated by the adjustable current of the motor.
Open position
If enough water is dosed the brewer runs counter clockwise to the open position.
Waste wipe
The brewer runs through, herewith the lower piston moves to the top position. Now the brewer starts running clockwise and the coffee cake is swiped from the piston into the waste bucket.
Back to home
After swiping the coffee cake away, the brewer runs in the clock wise direction to the home position.
Start/home position
The brewer is ready for a new cycle.

components.title: Remove the brewer
components.text:
Required
Use the following parts to perform the procedure:
• Blue brewer key
• Green service key
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Tear off the filter paper on the left and right of the brewer.
2. Insert the service key in the door.
3. In the Service menu tap the [Replace filter paper] button. ▪ The brewer chamber will move up to the open position.
4. Remove the service key from the door.
5. Remove the brewer chamber by pulling it in the direction of the arrow.
6. Remove the remaining old filter paper from the brewer. ▪ Lift the transport wheels with the cantilever if needed.
7. Remove the nozzle / outlet pipe from the brewer.
8. Take the brewer out of the machine. First tilt the lower part of the brewer towards you to release the main shaft from the motor interlocking.
▪ Tilting the lower part about 10 cm is enough.
9. Lift the brewer a little to release the studs from the suspension and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.

components.title: Add-on water CoEx XL (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
If an add-on water valve is installed in the hot water circuit, the machine can add extra water to an Americano recipe. The medium cabinet models use an additional valve on the open boiler.
For information on the installation of the add-on water option, refer to the installation instructions in the Appendix (on page 157).
Overview Add-on water connection (medium model)
The outlet nozzle (A) adds the water directly in the cup. The hose (B) is connected to the add-on water valve HW+ (D) on the valve stack on the open boiler.

components.title: Add-on water CoEx XL (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
If an add-on water valve (HW+) (D) is installed in the hot water circuit, the machine can add extra water to an Americano recipe.
The hose (B) is connected to the add-on water inlet (A) on the side of the CoEx XL to inject the extra water in the coffee stream.
For information on the installation of the add-on water option, refer to the installation instructions in the Appendix (on page 150).

components.title: Remove and install the CoEx® brewer
components.text:
Remove the brewer
Perform the following steps:
1. Loosen the brewer outlet from the brewer.
2. Locate the fixation handle on the brewer.
3. Push the fixation handle upwards and, while keeping the handle in the upward position, pull and lift the brewer in the direction of the arrow out of the coffee machine.
Install the brewer
Perform the following steps:
1. Make sure the brewer bracket in the coffee machine is clean.
2. Place the brewer on the bracket and push the brewer firmly in the bracket until you hear a click.
• Make sure that the fixation handle is in the down position.

components.title: Place the brewer
components.text:
Before installing, make sure the brewer chamber is still in the open position.
▪ If needed, adjust the position of the main shaft to fit the motor interlocking.
2. Place the studs at the back of the brewer in both suspension holes.
3. Lower the brewer down and make sure that the main shaft fits the motor interlocking.
▪ Some force is needed to lock the brewer properly.
4. Place the nozzle / outlet pipe on the brewer.
5. Guide the filter paper through the brewer, lift the transport wheels with the cantilever if needed.
▪ for details, see section Change filter paper.
6. Install the brewer chamber. Press the brewer chamber with the two pins into position.
7. Insert the service key in the door.
8. In the Service menu tap the [Replace filter paper] button. ▪ This will move the brewer through a cycle. Check if the filter paper is being transported properly and runs smoothly.

components.title: Clamp force adjustment
components.text:
Readjusting the clamp fore is necessary when too much water leaks between the brewer and the brewer chamber. This is the case when the filter paper becomes wet, more the 10 mm around the brewer chamber. Nevertheless, when the clamp force is adjusted to high, excessive wear can occur or the brewer motor can get stuck.
Adjust the brewer chamber clamp force as follows:
1. Open the machine door.
2. Tear the filter paper in front of the brewer and behind the brewer.
3. Remove the brewer from the machine.
4. Turn the brewer piston up using the Uni-key until the brewer chamber flips over.
5. Remove the filter paper from the brewer. Place a new piece of filter paper between the brewer and the brewer chamber.
6. Move the brewer piston in the upper position (connecting rods in line).
7. Turn the adjustment nut on top of the H-frame clockwise, until filter paper is just clamped between brewer and brewer chamber. The brewer chamber may not be pushed onto the brewer during the adjustment.
8. Turn the nut ½ - 1 turn clockwise.
9. Place the brewer in the machine
10. Place the filter paper according to the procedure in the user’s manual.
11. Check the operation of the brewer by selecting a coffee consumption.
Take notice of the following things: When the brewer chamber clamp force is set too low, water is leaking between the brewer and the brewer chamber. Turn the adjustment nut one quarter of a turn clockwise. The clamp force is set too high when the brewer piston does not move smoothly in the down position (during lifting of the brewer chamber). Turn the adjustment nut one quarter of a turn counter-clockwise. Check operation of the brewer again.
12. Close the machine door.

components.title: Removal and placement of the CoEx XL brewer
components.text:
Removal procedure
Perform the following steps to remove the brewer:
1. To remove the brewer from the coffee machine, place four fingers in the lower grip (1). With your thumb, push and hold down the locking grip (2) and pull the brewer from the mounting frame in the direction of the arrow (3).
Placement procedure
Perform the following steps to install the brewer:
1. Make sure the inside of the brewer mounting frame in the coffee machine is clean.
2. Insert the brewer into the mounting frame and push until it locks.
▪ All other connections are made automatically.
▪ The brewer will initialize once when the first coffee dispense is started. All brewer parts are moved to the correct starting position first.

components.title: Upper piston / filter head
components.text:
The upper piston, also known as filter head, is mounted in the top of the CoEx® brewer. This upper piston is removable with the fixation knob on the top of the brewer.
Upper piston internal layout
1. Quad ring (spare part)
2. Upper piston
3. Spring (yellow filter head only)
4. Pressure switch
5. Coffee restriction
6. O-Ring
7. U-cup sealing
8. Mesh holder
9. Filter mesh
10. Screws
Remove and install the upper piston
This upper piston is removable with the fixation knob on the top of the brewer.
1. To remove the filter head, turn the knob clockwise.
2. To fit on the brewer: First place the complete upper piston in the right position, then turn the knob counter clockwise.

components.title: Paper transport distance
components.text:
To prevent that old coffee remains in the brewer chamber, during the transportation of the filter paper, the distance between the layers of coffee residue can be adjusted. Especially for large dosing quantities of coffee this can be necessary. Nevertheless the distance between the layers should not be adjusted too big, to prevent unnecessary loss of paper (more often replacement of the paper reel).
The paper transport is adjusted correct when: After transport of the filter paper, no coffee remains in the brewer chamber. The distance between the layers of coffee residue is between 5 – 10 mm.
Adjust the paper transport as follows:
1. Hold the adjustment bolt and loosen the lock nut.
2. Turn the adjustment bolt counter-clockwise when coffee residue remains in the brewer chamber / Turn the adjustment bolt clockwise when the distance between the layers of coffee residue is too big.
3. Tighten the lock nut.
4. Check the operation of the paper transport.
5. Check the distance between the layers of coffee residue.
6. Place the service key in the door switch. The machine is switched on now.
7. Take at least 4x consumptions to test the paper transport distance.
8. Check the functioning of the machine by taking a test drink (coffee). Place a cup or a jug underneath the nozzle to collect the hot test drink.

components.title: Replace service parts in the brewer (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
The only serviceable parts in the brewer that need to be replaced after 50.000 brewing cycles (or 2 years) are:
1. the coffee filter assembly with seals.
2. the inner cylinder.
3. the inlet filter assembly with seals.
A complete set is available as spare part set.
The CoEx XL serial number (visible on a heat- and water resistant label on top of the brewer gear box) contains the manufacturing date. The number format is year-week-sequence number.
Procedure
Follow the steps to replace the service parts.
1. Before removing the brewer from the machine, first place the brewer in the Service position. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this, check the section Place brewer in service position (on page 66).
2. Remove the brewer from the machine and remove the cover from the brewer. Check the chapter 'Remove and clean the brewer' in the User manual for details.
Remove inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove one screw (1) that secures the inlet filter. (M4/ Length=16mm)
2. Turn the inlet filter clockwise (2) to release the bayonet locking.
3. Loosen and remove the inlet filter from the piston.
Remove inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Remove 1 screw that secures the inner cylinder. (M4/ Length=16mm).
2. Turn the brewer around again.
3. Slide the inner cylinder (1) out of the outer cylinder. Tilt (2) and remove it from the brewer.
Replace coffee filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Push the cylinder down by hand.
2. If the cylinder is locked, locate the clutches on the left (L) and right (R) side. Pull the right clutch up (or push from the back) and, at the same time, push the left clutch down. The cylinder can now move freely. Move it down to access the coffee filter.
3. Place the brewer in vertical position with the brewer locking grip facing upwards.
4. Locate the 2 screws in between the gears. Loosen and remove the 2 screws. (3.5/Length=8mm)
5. Remove the old coffee filter.
6. Place the new coffee filter. ▪ Make sure that the (coffee) water connectors are in line with each other
▪ When needed, turn the coffee filter slightly to fit the square filter shaft into the drive gear.
7. Secure the coffee filter with 2 screws.
Install inner cylinder
Follow this procedure:
1. Place the brewer on a flat surface as shown in the picture. Push the cylinder against the coffee filter.
2. Lower the inner cylinder inside the brewer and tilt it around the piston.
3. Slide it inside the outer cylinder.
4. Turn the brewer upside down. Secure the inner cylinder with 1 screw (M4x16).
Install inlet filter
Follow this procedure:
1. Position the new inlet filter. ▪ Align it with the transparent water coupling (inset 1).
▪ Lower the filter on the bayonet locking (inset 2) and turn the filter to lock.
▪ Secure the inlet filter with 1 screw (3). (M4/ Length=16mm)
2. Finished, the service parts are installed.
3. Place the cover and install the brewer in the coffee machine.

components.title: Controlling coffee/espresso pressure switch
components.text:
With the unique patented system the CoEx®-brewer can make Coffee and espresso consumptions in one brewing system. The pressure for coffee and espresso is different, coffee is made with 3 - 4 bar pressure, espresso with 9 bar pressure.
The volume of a consumption is easily changeable in the software settings in the machine.
The duration time that the water is in contact with the coffee powder is a very important factor in the performance of the brewer and is about the same for coffee and espresso. The optimal water-coffee contact time is 15 - 25 seconds.
To achieve this value a restriction in the system must be used. By the combination of a higher pressure, lower volume and an equal coffee contact time the flow for espresso must be much smaller than the flow for coffee. In the following figures the solution for making these two beverages in one system is shown.
1. Coffee flow When coffee is chosen, the start flow is relative low and will not activate the pressure switch. (Spring is strong enough to keep pressure switch in coffee position). The coffee passes the primary restriction and can then flow through the large coffee channel.
2. Espresso flow When espresso is chosen, at first the flow is high and will activate the pressure switch. (Spring is not strong enough to keep pressure switch in Coffee position). The coffee channel is closed and the espresso is forced through the secondary restriction, reducing the flow and increasing the pressure to 9 bar.
This different pressure between coffee and espresso is only used in the B2C espresso machines. The CoEx® machines used
as paperless fresh brew has no spring to switch between coffee or espresso pressure.
The upper piston is marked with a colored dot that refers to the hole size(s) and pressure switch.
