components.title: Remove the brewer chamber
components.text:
The brewer chamber needs to be removed weekly for cleaning. If the brewer is in the open position, the brewer chamber can be removed.
Make sure the pins are fixed correctly by placing the brewer chamber back.

components.title: Unlock the brewer
components.text:
In rare situations the brewer system can lock itself. If, for instance, the door of the coffee machine is opened during a coffee brewing cycle the brewer is halted for safety reasons and can remain in an unknown position.
1. Remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Remove the cover.
3. Turn the gear (1) and check if the piston will move up and down (see arrows) on the two lead screw piston transports.
4. Install the brewer in the coffee machine and dispense a coffee.

components.title: Replace seals in lower piston
components.text:
Required tool
Screw driver
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Unscrew the bolt (1) of the brewer and loosen the two other bolts (2).
2. Loosen the lower bolts (2) only 1.5 turns. Do not remove them.
3. Pull the left and right housing apart on each side of the cylinder (1) and pull the cylinder and piston upwards out of the brewer (2).
4. Remove the piston from the cylinder.
5. Replace the parts (see next nextion) and install in reversed order.

components.title: Place brewer in service position (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter must be pulled out of the coffee chamber first. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this. Check the section CoEx XL service position (on page 122) for details.
If the option is not available in the Service Menu, it needs to be done manually.
1. Open the door and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) counter clockwise.
4. The piston with inlet filter will move to the lowest position.

components.title: Place brewer in service position (CoEx XL Small)
components.text:
To replace all serviceable parts, the inlet filter must be pulled out of the coffee chamber first. A service option in the Service Menu can help to do this. Check the section CoEx XL service position (on page 116) for details.
If the option is not available in the Service Menu, it needs to be done manually.
1. Open the door and remove the brewer from the coffee machine.
2. Hold the brewer upside down.
3. Turn the main gear (1) counter clockwise.
4. The piston with inlet filter will move to the lowest position.

components.title: Seals
components.text:
The brewer contains two pistons, the upper piston (better known as filter head) and the lower piston. There are three sealing rings responsible for sealing of the pressure room: two in the lower piston and one in the upper piston.
1. Lower piston
2. Sealing ring (lower piston)
3. U-cup sealing ring - RED (lower piston)
4. U-cup sealing ring - BLUE (upper piston)
5. Upper piston / filter head
Hot water enters the cylinder (through the lower piston) between the two sealing rings in the piston. The mix of water and coffee powder will be filtered by the mesh in the upper piston and then leave the cylinder. The sealing in the upper piston and the lower sealing in the piston have to resist the pressure of the hot water during the brewing process (10 bars). The shape of the selected u-cup ring (3) avoids the coffee grains scratching the cylinder. The upper sealing ring (2) does not have to resist a high pressure but is only a scraping ring.

components.title: Calibrate the brewer / water flow meter (CoEx XL Medium)
components.text: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the amount of water and is calibrated in the factory. When the water flow meter is replaced, it needs to be calibrated once. The system needs to 'know' how much water is entering the brewer and how to position the needle in the flow regulator to make sure the amount of water is correct. Check the procedure in the Calibrations (see Calibration of Water flow meter on page 125) section for more details.

components.title: Calibrate the brewer / water flow meter (CoEx XL Small)
components.text: The water flow meter (water counter) measures the amount of water and is calibrated in the factory. When the water flow meter is replaced, it needs to be calibrated once. The system needs to 'know' how much water is entering the brewer and how to position the needle in the flow regulator to make sure the amount of water is correct. Check the procedure in the Calibrations (see Calibration of Water flow meter on page 119) section for more details.

components.title: Replace the flow regulator
components.text:
Purpose
There is no need to replace the flow regulator. Regular cleaning of the machine will keep the flow regulator clean and working properly. Replace only if requested by the service department.
Required
Use the following parts to perform the procedure:
• Philips screwdriver
• Flow regulator replacement set with part number 9ZBR108.

components.title: Remove the flow regulator
components.text:
Procedure
1. Remove the CoEx XL brewer from the machine.
2. Remove the cover from the brewer.
3. Make sure the brewer is clean. ▪ Clean with warm water (a mild detergent may be added) and make sure to remove any leftover coffee grains.
4. Remove the screw (A) that secures the outlet support (C).
5. Loosen the flexible connections (B) and remove the outlet support.
6. Remove the two screws (A) from the flow regulator (B).
7. Lift the spindle end (A) from the brewer frame. ▪ If needed, rotate the spindle end first to release it from the brewer frame.
▪ Unlock the spindle gear (B) from the guide (C).
8. Slide and lift the flow regulator (D) from the regulator pipe (E) where it connects to the filter.
9. Pull the spindle gear (A) away from the flow regulator (B) until the needle (C) is visible.
10. Turn the spindle gear (A) 180° -in either direction- and unlock it from the needle (B).

components.title: Install a new flow regulator
components.text:
Use the new flow regulator (C) and connect the spindle gear (A) to the needle (B).
2. Turn the spindle gear (A) 180° -in either direction-to lock it to the needle (B).
3. Push the spindle gear (A) into the regulator (C) and check that the spindle gear is locked to the needle (B) as shown in the picture.
▪ Note that the needle locking is visible.
4. Pump the spindle gear in and out a few times to make sure the needle in the flow regulator can move freely.
5. Position the spindle gear (A) under the inlet water hose (B) first.
6. Insert the flow regulator (C) in the regulator pipe (D).
7. Insert the spindle end (E) in the frame at the back of the brewer.
▪ Rotate the spindle end, if needed, to adjust the length and fit it in the frame.
8. Push down the middle of the spindle gear (A) to lock it in the guide (F) inside the frame.
9. Secure the flow regulator (A) with two screws (B). ▪ Do not tighten the screws too hard.
10. Connect the two flexible connections (A) of the outlet support (B) to the flow regulator (C) and secure with one screw (D).
11. The replacement is finished.
12. Place the cover on the brewer and install the brewer in the machine.

components.title: Test the flow regulator
components.text:
Place the service key.
2. Login in the Service Menu.
3. Tap the [HARDWARE] button.
4. Make sure the waste bucket is completely dry. ▪ During execution of the test recipe in the next step, check for water in the waste bucket.
5. Tap the [Test espresso recipe] button. ▪ Check that:
a. no water leaks in the waste bucket during execution of the test recipe.
b. at the end of the recipe, the needle moves to the flush position and releases a small amount of water. This amount of water is visible in the waste bucket.

components.title: Grinder
components.text: The coffee machine can contain one or two grinders. They are mounted inside the machine on the canister plate.

components.title: Ingredient canisters (Instant Medium / Instant Small)
components.text:
The canisters are provided with a metal or plastic auger. The metal auger is used for instant coffee, instant tea and leaf tea.
The plastic auger is used for the other ingredients. Special augers are available for special ingredients or low gram throws.
All canisters are driven by a 24VDC 120RPM motor.

components.title: General
components.text:
The D-grinder uses high performance grinder discs that give a consistent grind and operates at about twice the speed of the Schaerer grinder to grind beans for coffee and espresso. This means that the same amount of ground coffee is created in half the time. Check the specifications at the end of this chapter for more details. The D-grinder is easy to clean and settings (like grinding degree) are maintained when the grinder is opened for cleaning. The grinding degree of the D-grinder is not measured in pins and teeth but displayed in an indicator window on the grinder. The indicator shows a scale from 0 to 12 (actual degrees divided by 10). The D-grinder is set to a default grinding degree of 6 in the factory. Note that the type of beans used and (local) flavor expectations may require a different setting of the grinder in the coffee machine.
1. Auger 10. Grinder motor drive
2. Grinder house top assembly 11. Grinding degree adjustment screw
3. Upper grinding disc (stationary) 12. Grinding degree scale window
4. Screws upper grinding disc 13. Grinder adjustment cover
5. Screws lower grinding disc 14. Screws worm wheel assembly
6. Lower grinding disc (rotating) 15. Adjustment wheel
7. Grinder base / Motor cover 16. Grinder outlet
8. Grinder stand 17. Drive shaft
9. Grinder house 18. Grinding disc assembly bottom
The grinder unit consists of the top assembly (2) that contains the stationary –non moving-upper grinding disc (3). The top assembly is secured to the grinder house using a bayonet catch for easy access. The grinder house (9) contains the bottom assembly with the rotating lower grinding disc (6). By adjusting the lower grinding disc up and down, the air gap between the two grinder discs can be set very accurately. The gap between the two grinder discs determines the grain size of the ground coffee also known as the grinding degree. The grinding degree is set manually by rotating the adjustment wheel (15) with an adjustment screw (11). This screw is accessible when the grinder is installed in the coffee machine. The adjustment wheel contains a grinding degree scale that is visible through a small window (12). A 24-volt motor in the grinder base powers the lower grinding disc via a gear box to the drive shaft (17).

components.title: Change the grinding degree
components.text:
The grinding degree can be adjusted without removing the grinder from the coffee machine.
The actual grinding degree is visible in a small indicator window in the bottom left of the grinder.
1. Adjust the grinding degree with the (Philips type) screw, accessible on the bottom right of the grinder base.
▪ Turn left (+) for a coarser grinding / higher number.
▪ Turn right (-) for a finer grinding / lower number.
▪ Turn the screw in the desired direction and check the indicator to see the current grinding degree.
Set the grinding degree to the value 6 (factory default) or to the preferred value that was already known.
Take a test beverage to test for taste and write down the finally set grinding degree for future reference.
The outer areas of the scale are marked in red (values lower than 1.5 and higher than 10.5).
This is only needed once (or when installing a new grinder or new grinder discs).

components.title: Remove and place the grinder
components.text:
To access the grinder, first remove the bean canister. ▪ The grinder is placed and positioned on grinder stands inside the grinder base and is secured only using the driving shaft.
2. To remove the grinder, lift it from the grinder base in the direction of the arrow.
3. Place the grinder in the grinder base and make sure the grinder outlet points in the right direction.
▪ Rotate the grinder auger to allow the drive shaft to ‘fit’ and move down completely. The drive shaft must ‘fit’ in the motor drive.

components.title: Clean the grinder
components.text:
Regular (monthly) cleaning of the grinder is recommended to prevent clogging of old ground coffee inside the grinder house.
Also, burned beans and ‘foreign’ objects (like wood or stones) can block the grinder and need to be removed.
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Remove the grinder from the machine.
2. Open the grinder house.
3. Clean the grinder discs and the inside of the grinder house (do not forget to clean the gap around the discs).
4. Close the grinder house.
5. Install the grinder in the machine.

components.title: Replace the grinder discs
components.text:
The upper and lower discs are identical.
The screws in the lower and the upper disc are NOT identical.
Required tools
• Philips screwdriver
Procedure
Perform the following steps:
1. Remove the grinder from the machine.
2. Remove the grinder outlet. ▪ spread the two fixation clips (1) that secure the outlet to the grinder.
▪ slide the outlet in the direction of the arrow (2) and remove it from the grinder.
3. Remove the grinder house top assembly. ▪ Turn the cover of the top assembly in the direction of the arrow (clockwise!) to unlock the bayonet catch and remove the top assembly from the grinder.
4. Remove screws from upper grinding disc.
5. Remove the upper disc.
6. Before placing the new upper grinding disc make sure that the mounting surface is clean.
7. Place the upper grinder disc.
8. Secure the upper disc with three screws.
Tighten the screws gently, but firmly.
9. Loosen and remove the three screws in the lower disc.
10. Remove the lower disc.
11. Clean up the grinder house and make sure that the mounting surface for the lower grinding disc is clean (to prevent a different grinding degree).
12. Place the new lower grinding disc.
13. Secure the lower grinding disc with three screws.
Tighten the screws gently, but firmly.
14. Close the grinder house. ▪ Install grinder house top assembly.
▪ Place the grinder house top assembly on top of the grinder and turn it in the direction of the arrow (counter clockwise!) to close and lock it to the grinder house.
15. Install grinder outlet. ▪ Slide the grinder outlet in the direction of the arrow on the outside of the grinder house and make sure the locking clips of the outlet lock properly.

components.title: Readjust the D-grinder (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The D-grinder has been set in the factory to the default grinding degree of 6, this number corresponds to a gap between the two grinder discs of about 0.25 mm.
Readjustment is possible if this number, shown in the little window on the grinder, does not match with the actual gap between the grinder discs. This can happen :
• when new grinder discs are installed.
• after the initial break-in period of the grinder discs (after grinding beans for 1000 cups of coffee).
Required tools
• Torx 20 screwdriver
Procedure
Perform the following steps
1. Remove the adjustment cover. ▪ Bend the four locking clips (1) in the direction of the arrows and pull the adjustment cover (2) from the grinder house.
2. Remove the screws that secure the adjustment wheel. ▪ Pull the adjustment wheel from the drive shaft in the direction of the arrow. The adjustment disc is now visible.
3. To be able to turn the adjustment disc, insert two screws and give them a few turns.
4. Turn the adjustment disc gently in the direction of the arrow until the two grinding discs touch each other.
5. Check that the drive shaft cannot be turned anymore. ▪ The grinder discs are now reset to 0 (zero).
6. Remove the two support screws from the adjustment disc. ▪ Make sure not to change the current position of the adjustment disc.
7. Slide the adjustment wheel onto the drive shaft. The adjustment wheel contains a restrictor (1) that fits in a slot on the outside of the grinder house (2). The restriction slot limits the rotation of the adjustment wheel to 120º.
▪ Push the adjustment wheel down the shaft and turn it clockwise until the restrictor is in the left corner of the slot of the grinder house.
8. A second check: make sure that the number 0 of the scale on the adjustment wheel is positioned above the small vertical mark in the outside of the grinder house near the grinder outlet.
9. Secure the adjustment wheel with three screws. ▪ Tighten the screws gently but firmly.
10. Place the cover. The numbers 1 and 2 are embossed on the bottom outside of the adjustment cover. Position the number 1 in line with the grinder outlet. Position the number 2 in line with the grinder outlet for a grinder in door only.
▪ Slide the adjustment cover in the direction of the arrows and make sure that the four clips lock properly to the ledges on the outside of the grinder house.
11. The readjustment is now finished. Continue with the section Grinding degree (see Change the grinding degree on page 70) to set the grinder to the preferred grinding degree that was already noted down.

components.title: Mixer (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The mixer consists of a mixer motor, a mixer propeller and a mixer house. The mixer is controlled by the control board and ensures a correct mixing of the ingredient(s) and water. By the rotation of the mixer propeller, air is mixed with the water and ingredient(s) and a foam layer is formed. This will improve the taste and the appearance of the consumption.
Motor specification: 24VDC, 14.000 RPM. In case of a blockage, a safety is actuated on the IO board and the message “mixer blocked” is shown in the screen.
A restricted inlet diameter of the mixer house is used to create a nice flow in the mixer bowl.

black for the pressure boiler system, grey for the open boiler system.

components.title: Mixer (Filterfresh Medium / Filterfresh Small)
components.text:
The mixer consists of a mixer motor, a mixer propeller and a mixer house. The mixer is controlled by the control board and ensures a correct mixing of the ingredient(s) and water. By the rotation of the mixer propeller, air is mixed with the water and ingredient(s) and a foam layer is formed. This will improve the taste and the appearance of the consumption.
Motor specification: 24VDC, 14.000 RPM. In case of a blockage, a safety is actuated on the IO board and the message “mixer blocked” is shown in the screen.
A restricted inlet diameter of the mixer house is used to create a nice flow in the mixer bowl.
Overview of mixer parts (small and medium models)
1. Suction trap
2. Adapter (*)
3. Seal
4. Mixer bayonet catch
5. Mixer house (*)
6. Mixer propeller
7. Mixer motor *) Mixer house and adapter colors:
black for the pressure boiler system, grey for the open boiler system.

components.title: Canister plate beans canister (CEC, FEC, XEA)
components.text:
Remove the canister plate bean canister
Perform the following steps:
1. Pull the canister lock in the direction of the arrow to release the bean canister from the grinder base.
2. Lift the canister from the grinder base and out of the coffee machine.
3. Install the bean canister - Place the bean canister on the grinder base and push the canister lock in the direction of the arrow.

components.title: Coffee beans canisters
components.text: Depending on the model, the coffee machine can contain coffee bean canisters on the canister plate or inside the door.

components.title: Ingredient canisters (CEC, FEC, XEA)
components.text:
The canisters are provided with a metal or plastic auger. The metal auger is used for instant coffee, instant tea and leaf tea.
The plastic auger is used for the other ingredients. Special augers are available for special ingredients or low gram throws.
All canisters are driven by a 24VDC 120RPM motor.

components.title: Power supply
components.text:
The power supply is located at the backplate of the machine behind the ingredient canisters. The mains voltage is connected to the power supply. This board supplies power to the I/O board and to all other electrical components. For over voltage protection, the power supply has been equipped with a fuse.

components.title: Cup sensor (CoEx Medium)
components.text:
The cup sensor senses a cup on the cup stand. A maximum of two cup sensors can be connected in the machine. One for the right and one for the left outlet.
A cup must be placed on the correct position on the cup stand before the start button is available and the cycle can start. The sensitivity of the sensor is adjustable in the Service Menu, see Cup sensor (see Cup sensors on page 119).
Cup sensor PCB (all small and medium models)
The sensor housing may vary, depending on machine type. For further details, check the spare parts manual.

menu.title: Inserting service key
menu.text: Insert the service key and turn this key a quarter turn. Be aware of the following: • Possible moving parts inside the machine, beware of trapped fingers if the service key is placed when the door is open. • Beware of hot parts and hot liquid inside the machine, even after the power is disconnected.
steps: Possible moving parts inside the machine, beware of trapped fingers if the service key is placed when the door is open.
Beware of hot parts and hot liquid inside the machine, even after the power is disconnected.
notes: Inserting the service key gives electrical power to components.

menu.title: Filling & Cleaning – door open
menu.text: After the door is opened, the service mode is shown on the screen. 1. [Exit] button 2. Description of the active menu 3. [Login] button 4. Available options 5. [Back] button 6. System messages 7. [Next page] button – option 8. [Previous page] button – option Buttons that require a part of the machine to be active are grey and do not work as long as the service key is not inserted. For example: the cleaning cycle only works when the service key is in the door. (This key is in the machine for safety reasons. In accordance with CE, components may not be active when the door is open, unless a safety key is used.) The menu options shown here depend on the model and are explained in detail in the following chapters.

menu.title: Daily rinse / Daily cleaning cycle
menu.text: The rinse cycle needs to be done at least once a day. Place a jug or bin under the outlet nozzles before starting the rinse cycle. Check the User manual for more details. NOTE - This option can be disabled in the Service Menu Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Cleaning Settings (not recommended and only if an alternative procedure is used as a daily cleaning procedure).

menu.title: Brewer cleaning cycle
menu.text: The brewer cleaning cycle needs to be done at least once a week. Tapping the brewer cleaning button will show a new screen with instructions. Follow the instructions and finish the whole procedure to reset the cleaning counter. If a "cleaning error" message appears, run the cleaning cycle again. Check the User manual for more details.
notes: Always complete the entire brewer cleaning cycle. If the cleaning cycle is interrupted, for instance by pressing the [CANCEL] button, the cleaning cycle must be repeated in full.
This option can be disabled in the section Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Cleaning Settings (not recommended and only if an alternative procedure is used for this function).

menu.title: Menu Layouts
menu.text: Login > Presentation > Vending menu layout / Jug menu layout This menu contains information and settings for the menu items, images and videos displayed on the screen of the coffee machine. Menu Layouts The menu items can be altered. First select the layout that needs to be changed: • [Vending (Cups) Menu Layout] • [Jug Menu Layout] To change the order of the menu items on the user screen, press and hold the [image] and drag the image to the new location. • If more than one category is configured, first tap the correct [category] button. • Swipe up and down to scroll to see all menu items. To see and change the (translated) names and image of the menu item: 1. Tap the [pencil] button in the desired menu item: ▪ To change the (translated) menu item name, tap the [pencil] button of the menu item. ▪ To change the image of the menu item, tap the [<] or [>] button and browse to the desired menu item image. 2. Tap the [Back] button to exit. ▪ Changes are saved immediately.

menu.title: Media
menu.text: Login > Presentation > Standby / Distributing / Logo / Background Images General • With the exception of the background and the info panel images, all other images can be handled remotely using ConnectMe. A valid ConnectMe account is needed. • Uploading videos to the coffee machine is only possible using ConnectMe. Video specifications Maximum video file size 300 Mb Supported formats mp4, mov, wmv, avi, qt, asf, x-msvideo, x-ms-wmv Image specifications Avy Maximum image file size 1 Mb Allowed image formats .png / .jpg / .gif (static) Display resolution 1920 x 1080 Image resolutions: • Standby images • 1920 x 1080 • Distributing images • 1200 x 671 • Logo image • 200 x 70 • Info panel image • 1200 x 700 • Background image • 1920 x 1080 For each image type, the following functions are available: • Tap the [Load <media> from USB] button to load one or more images from a USB stick, inserted in the USB port of the machine. • Tap the [Trash] button to remove an image from the machine. • To change the sequence of images shown on screen, press and hold the [image] button, then drag the item to the new position. • Tap the [Enable/Disable] switch to determine of the specific image will be shown or not. • Tap the [clock] button to change the display time (in seconds) of this specific image. Logo If the Logo image resolutions are specified in the table above, a user logo can be displayed on the screen. • Tap the [Select active logo] switch to select a logo if more than one logo is available on the machine. ▪ Only one logo can be shown at the same time. Standby media Standby images are displayed on the screen if the coffee machine is not used (is a screensaver). Standby after time delay time after the last dispensed beverage and the display of the first standby image. • Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the time. • Standby images are not shown when disabled. Show only touchless QR as standby images when enabled, a QR code is shown. A smartphone can be used for selection of a drink. Video volume tap the slider to adjust the volume of the standby video -- optional. Distributing media Distributing images are displayed during the preparation and dispense of the selected beverage. Video volume tap the slider to adjust the volume of the distributing video -- optional. Images can be connected to all consumptions (generic) or to specific products / recipes. 1. menu.title: Touchless Interface
menu.text: Login > Presentation > Touchless Instead of using the touchscreen to select a drink, the screen displays a QR code that can be scanned by a smartphone. The code will direct the user to a web page with a selection of the drinks available on that machine. After placing a cup and selection of the desired drink on the smartphone, the machine will prepare the drink as usual. Touchless enabled tap the [switch] to enable the Touchless Interface. A machine specific QR code is displayed on the main menu. When enabled, the following options are also available: Show only touchless QR as standby image tap the [switch] to show the QR code instead of standby images if the machine is not used. Save printable QR to USB to save a QR code image. First, insert a USB stick in the USB port of the machine and then tap the [Save] button to store the image on the USB stick.
notes: The machine needs to be connected to the internet to use this functionality.

menu.title: Filling & Cleaning - logged in
menu.text: Main menu -> Maintenance -> Brewer cleaning cycle. The weekly cleaning cycle has to be run at least once a week. Pressing the weekly cleaning button brings up a new screen with instructions. Follow them and go through the whole procedure so the cleaning counter is reset. If a cleaning error message appears, run the cleaning cycle again. See the user manual for more information.
notes: Always run the brewer cleaning cycle right through. If the cycle is interrupted, for instance by pressing [CANCEL], the whole cleaning cycle has to be repeated.

menu.title: Cleaning settings
menu.text: Login > Filling & Cleaning This menu contains information and settings (depending on model, type of configuration and login level) for the available cleaning messages. A message is displayed as a warning when the set time specified in the warning interval has expired. The machine will continue to work. If the time set in the critical interval has expired, the message is displayed and the machine is disabled completely. Cleaning error If a cleaning error message is displayed, tap the [Reset] button. The machine beeps, and the brewer cleaning message is cleared from the screen. Daily rinse [Enable/disable] switch - when disabled, the "Daily rinse needed" message is never displayed and the button is not available on the Filling & Cleaning menu (not recommended). When enabled, the following settings are available: Last executed shows date and time of the last daily rinse operation. Tap the [Reset] button to set it to the current date and time. • The daily cleaning procedure also resets this counter. Critical interval the message is displayed as an error after this number of hours has passed since the last daily rinse (default: 36). Brewer cleaning [Enable/disable] switch - when disabled, the "Rinse brewer with tablet" message is never displayed and the button is not available on the Filling & Cleaning menu (not recommended). When enabled, the following settings are available: Last executed shows date and time of the last brewer cleaning. Tap the [Reset] button to set it to the current date and time. • A brewer cleaning cycle resets this counter. Critical interval the message is displayed as an error after this number of hours has passed since the last brewer cleaning (default: 216). Waste bin fill level monitoring [Enable/disable] switch - when disabled, the "Waste bin full / Empty waste bin" message is never displayed. The button is not available on the Filling & Cleaning menu (not recommended). Reset when waste bin is removed for more than 4 seconds. When enabled, the waste bin switch is monitored. When the bin is removed for more than 4 seconds, the fill level is reset to zero. Current fill weight displays the calculated current filling level based on each coffee related dispense. Tap the [Reset] button to set the fill weight to zero. Critical level when the fill weight is more than this value, an error message is displayed. Tap the [pencil] button to change this level.

notes: Be sure the brewer is clean, and no cleaning agent or cleaning powder is left in the brewer.

menu.title: Canister settings (CEC, CND, FEC)
menu.text: Login > Filling & Cleaning > Fill level monitoring The coffee machine can show a message "Canister x almost empty" when the canister contents are running low. After calibrating once, the coffee machine knows the starting weight of the ingredient in the canister and the amount that is dispensed with every recipe. The machine calculates the available amount after every dispense and displays the message if the predefined percentage levels are reached. Fill level monitoring The message can be enabled/disabled for each canister. Track Fill Level tap the [switch] to enable the desired canister: • [green] = fill level monitored • [grey] = fill level not monitored Full weight shows the weight of the completely filled ingredient canister. • Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the full weight. Almost empty warning percentage filling level when the message "Canister x almost empty" is displayed. • Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the percentage. In the Service Menu, check the section Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Ingredient Canister for the actual calibrations.

menu.title: Cup sensors
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Cup sensors Cup sensor signal The signal of the sensors are read individually. This way the presence and visibility of a cup can be tested too. Cup sensor setting Tap the [Enable/Disable] switch to disable the sensor. When disabled, the machine works like there is no sensor. The sensitivity of the cup sensor is adjustable. The value can be adjusted between 0 and 4096. A higher value means less sensitive. So for detecting a transparent or dark colored cup the value must be set low. Measured shows the current measured value. Threshold value needed to trigger a cup present level. The message 'Place cup xxxx' is displayed (where xxxx will be left, right or middle) if this level is not reached. The default value is 100. This value gives the best detection for the most cup types. If there are two cup sensors in the machine, both are individually adjustable. Tap the [pencil] button to change the threshold value. Sensor 1 = Middle sensor. Sensor 2 = Right hand side sensor, hot (and cold -- optional) water.
notes: When disabled, drinks will be dispensed, even when no cup is placed.
Black cups or clear glass cups are not detectable, we advise to switch off the sensors if black cups or clear glass cups are used.

menu.title: Boiler(s) — CoEx Medium
menu.text: Current temperature Change temperature setting Login > Hardware > Boilers Shows the set and the actual temperature of the boiler(s) in degrees Celcius. Tap the [pencil] button to adjust the setting of the boiler. Recommended boiler temperature settings: Boiler Temperature Boiler 1 (pressure) 92 °C Boiler 2 (open) 91 °C The optimal temperature setting of the pressure boiler is 92 ºC. If no consumptions are made, the temperature in the boiler will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer.
notes: Sorte kopper eller klare glaskopper kan ikke detekteres, og vi anbefaler at slukke sensorerne, hvis der anvendes sorte kopper eller klare glaskopper.

menu.title: Calibration of canisters (CoEx Medium)
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Ingredient Canisters Calibrate Ingredient canisters Perform the following steps: 1. Fill up the ingredient canister as usual. 2. Weigh the complete filled canister. 3. Tap the Full weight [pencil] button of the desired ingredient canister and enter the weight. 4. If needed, tap the Almost empty warning [pencil] button to adjust the percentage (filling level) when the Canister almost empty message should be displayed. 5. Go back to the main menu and select the Hardware > Calibrations screen. 6. Select the desired ingredient canister and tap the [Calibrate] button. 7. Follow the steps on the screen and explained below. 8. Place a cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button. ▪ The product motor runs for 3 seconds (just to fill up the outlets). ▪ Empty the cup. ▪ The second screen is shown. 9. Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function. 10. Place the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button again. ▪ The product motor runs for 10 seconds at full speed. 11. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 12. Enter the weight of the cup contents in the field and empty the cup. ▪ Tap [Retry] to repeat the previous action. ▪ Tap [Next] to continue with the next step. 13. Place the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button again. ▪ The product motor runs for 10 seconds at 80% speed. 14. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 15. Enter the weight of the cup contents in the field. ▪ Tap [Retry] to repeat the previous action. ▪ Tap [Next] to continue with the next step. 16. Check the entered details and tap [Save] when correct. ▪ Tap [Restart] to repeat the full procedure for this canister. 17. The procedure is now finished. ▪ Repeat the Calibrate procedure for another canister. After calibration, the canister needs to be activated for monitoring. Check the section Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Canister Settings for more details.

If needed, tap the Almost empty warning [pencil] button to adjust the percentage (filling level) when the Canister almost empty message should be displayed. 5. Go back to the main menu and select the Hardware > Calibrations screen. 6. Select the desired ingredient canister and tap the [Calibrate] button. 7. Follow the steps on the screen and explained below. 8. Place a cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button. ▪ The product motor runs for 3 seconds (just to fill up the outlets). ▪ Empty the cup. ▪ The second screen is shown. 9. Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function. 10. Place the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button again. ▪ The product motor runs for 10 seconds at full speed. 11. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 12. Enter the weight of the cup contents in the field and empty the cup. ▪ Tap [Retry] to repeat the previous action. ▪ Tap [Next] to continue with the next step. 13. Place the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap the [Next] button again. ▪ The product motor runs for 10 seconds at 80% speed. 14. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 15. Enter the weight of the cup contents in the field. ▪ Tap [Retry] to repeat the previous action. ▪ Tap [Next] to continue with the next step. 16. Check the entered details and tap [Save] when correct. ▪ Tap [Restart] to repeat the full procedure for this canister. 17. The procedure is now finished. ▪ Repeat the Calibrate procedure for another canister. After calibration, the canister needs to be activated for monitoring. Check the section Login > Filling & Cleaning > Filling & Cleaning > Canister Settings for more details.

menu.title: Calibration of Water flow meter (CoEx Medium)
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Calibrations > Water flow meter When the pressure reducer or water flow meter is replaced, the water flow meter (water counter) needs to be calibrated. Follow the steps below. 1. Open and close the door of the coffee machine to display the service menu. 2. Tap the [Daily rinse] button to rinse the hoses/boilers and remove air from the system. 3. Login with the highest level. 4. Allow the boilers to heat up and make sure the ”Wait, Heating boiler” message is removed from the screen. 5. Adjust the pressure reducer with an espresso recipe. ▪ This is only needed if the pressure reducer was replaced. Check the Pressure reducer section for more details. 6. From the list with components, search for the Flow meter entry and tap the [Calibrate] button. ▪ The procedure steps to calibrate the water flow meter are shown on the screen and explained below. 7. Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function. ▪ or use a measuring cup. 8. Open the door of the machine. 9. Place the cup below the waste water outlets inside the machine. 10. Tap the [Next] button. ▪ Insert the service key in the door to enable the button. 11. The cup is filled with water. ▪ when finished, the 2nd part of the menu is displayed. 12. Measure the amount of water in the cup. 13. Tap the [Next] button and enter the amount in the field on the screen. The amount should be about 125 ml. ▪ if the actual amount differs more than 5 ml, tap [Retry] to repeat the calibration step. 14. Tap the [Save] button to save the current value and finish the Calibration. 15. Leave the service menu and return to the main menu of the coffee machine. 16. Test a hot water dispense and check if the amount is the same as specified in the hot water recipe.

steps: Open and close the door of the coffee machine to display the service menu.
Tap the [Daily rinse] button to rinse the hoses/boilers and remove air from the system.
Login with the highest level.
Allow the boilers to heat up and make sure the ”Wait, Heating boiler” message is removed from the screen.
Adjust the pressure reducer with an espresso recipe. ▪ This is only needed if the pressure reducer was replaced. Check the Pressure reducer section for more details.
From the list with components, search for the Flow meter entry and tap the [Calibrate] button.
The procedure steps to calibrate the water flow meter are shown on the screen and explained below.
Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function.
or use a measuring cup.
Place the cup below the hot water outlet.
Tap the [Next] button. ▪ Insert the service key in the door to enable the button.
The cup is filled with water. ▪ when finished, the 2nd part of the menu is displayed.

Tap the [Next] button and enter the amount in the field on the screen. The amount should be about 125 ml.
if the actual amount differs more than 5 ml, tap [Retry] to repeat the calibration step.

Leave the service menu and return to the main menu of the coffee machine.
Test a hot water dispense and check if the amount is the same as specified in the hot water recipe.

menu.text: In case the machine needs to be stored for a longer time, or needs to be transported (freezing weather, plane) the internal hoses and boilers needs to be emptied. menu.title: Empty pressure boilers (CoEx Medium / CoEx Small)
menu.text: Login > Hardware > Drain boilers In case the machine needs to be stored for a longer time, or needs to be transported (freezing weather, plane) the internal hoses and boilers need to be emptied. The boilers are emptied due to gravity. Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Switch off the machine and remove the power cord from the wall socket. 2. Close the connection to the water supply. 3. Remove the back cover plate from the machine. 4. Remove the plug from the metal elbow or T coupling right after the pump(s). See inset. 5. Connect a 6 mm hose to the elbow. ▪ Make sure the outlet of this hose ends in a large bucket, placed lower than the inlet valve of the machine. 6. Put the power cord back in the wall socket and switch the machine on. 7. Login in the service menu and tap [Hardware] > [Drain Boilers] > [Start]. 8. The procedure is now shown on the screen. 9. Place the service key and tap [Next] to start the draining process. ▪ The pumps will run for a short time, the 3-way valve opens to add air to the system. Slowly all water runs out of the boiler and hoses.

menu.title: Software (6.7.1)
menu.text: Login > Software Active configuration Shows the currently active configuration. Other configurations Shows all other configurations on this machine. Delete Delete a configuration file. Backup Tap the [Backup] button of the desired configuration file to create a backup copy. A copy of the configuration file with all settings is made. The back-up file name is the original name and an added timestamp (year, month, day and time). Original file name: <MODEL><VERSION>.mvq <MODEL> = Name and model machine, e.g. Lua_9235... <VERSION> = Version of the software, e.g. V9.... Backup file name: <MODEL><VERSION>_YYMMDDTIME.mvq YY = year, e.g. 20 = 2020 MM = month, e.g. 01 = January DD = day, eg. 04 = 4th day of the month Load configuration from USB Standard Device 0 is available (only if a USB stick is placed). It is possible to explore the maps in the stick to find the needed configuration file. The new loaded file from the stick is selected, loaded and set as active configuration automatically. Save configuration to USB This will save the current active file to the USB stick.
notes: pen Sie auf die Taste [Backup] der gewünschten Konfigurationsdatei, um eine Backup-Kopie zu erstellen. Eine Kopie der Konfigurationsdatei mit allen Einstellungen wird erstellt. Der Name der Sicherungsdatei ist der ursprüngliche Dateiname plus ein hinzugefügter Zeitstempel (Jahr, Monat, Tag und Uhrzeit).

menu.title: Scheduled Actions
menu.text: Login > Software > Scheduled actions Scheduler actions The following automatic actions can be set: • (Adaptive) Energy Save / Eco mode • Machine blocked • Free vend • Use other price list • Machine off • Mixer kick (do not change) • Daily rinse (do not change) Overview of the default (set in the factory) scheduler settings: Adaptive Energy Save If the coffee machine is connected to ConnectMe, the Energy Save mode can be made adaptive. In that case, ConnectMe monitors the use of the machine and optimizes the Energy Save values to be more in line with the actual use. Energy Save With the energy save settings, the machine can be switched to an energy saving mode (economic mode) during a period of time. During this time the boiler temperature drops to 65 ºC. When a user selects a drink, the machine will first heat to the normal temperature, before the machine is ready to give consumptions. During the warming up period the message "Heating Boiler" is shown. If the machine is not used for an hour the machine will go back to the energy save mode. Machine blocked During this set time, the functions on the front panel are blocked and not visible for the user. No consumptions can be chosen. The boiler(s) stay hot. (The service mode is still working). Switch to free vend A machine in pay mode can be switched to free vend during the set time. Check the Software -> Payment section to place the machine in Paid Mode. Use other price list In the set time the machine will switch to the other price list. Check the Products -> Price Settings section for more details. Machine off The machine is switched off during the set time. The display is completely black. The boiler elements are switched off. During this time the machine can only be activated in the service menu.

Active time zone shows the current time zone to enable automatic daylight saving settings. Tap the [Pencil] button to change this settings. Date shows the actual date. Tap the [Pencil] button to change this settings. Show clock in main menu when set to 'Disabled', the Clock is not displayed in the user menu.

Enter a valid 9 digit code and tap [Save]. ▪ More information about ConnectMe can be found in the ‘ConnectMe installation manual’ and 'User manual'.

menu.title: Payment
menu.text: Login > Software > Payment When a payment unit is installed / connected, payment settings are available to set the options of the payment system. Paid vend tap the desired mode: free vend or paid mode. Multi vend a payment system can run in multi vend or single vend: • Multi vend: select and dispense one or more consumptions. Your change or card will be returned after pressing the return button on change giver or card reader. • Singe vend: select and dispense one consumption. Your change or card is returned directly after dispense of the consumption. Overpay allowed in exact change enable to allow to insert more money as the highest consumption price. Not allowed means that it is not possible to insert more money as the highest consumption price. Selected currency tap to select the active currency. Price settings - In the Service Menu, check the section Login > Products > Settings > Price Settings for details about price lists. - In clock/time settings it is possible to automatically choose between price lists and free or paid mode for a certain period of time.

menu.title: Calibrations
menu.text: In this menu tab it is possible to calibrate the water flow meter (water counter) by following the steps: 1. Open and close the door of the coffee machine to display the service menu. 2. Tap the [Daily rinse] button to rinse the hoses/boilers and remove air from the system. 3. Login with the highest level. 4. Allow the boilers to heat up and make sure the ”Wait, Heating boiler” message is removed from the screen. 5. Adjust the pressure reducer with an espresso recipe. ▪ This is only needed when the pressure reducer was replaced. 6. From the menu, tap the selection [Calibrate]. The calibration menu is displayed showing all relevant steps. 7. Place a clean, empty cup on a scale and set the scale to 0 using the ‘tare’ function. ▪ or use a measuring cup. 8. Open the door of the machine. 9. Place the cup below the waste water outlets inside the machine. 10. Tap the [press here to start Calibration] button. 11. The cup is filled with water. ▪ when finished, the 2nd part of the menu is displayed. 12. Measure the amount of water in the cup. 13. Enter the amount in the field on the screen. The amount should be about 125 ml. ▪ if the actual amount differs more than 5 ml, first enter the amount and then repeat the calibration step. 14. Tap the [press here to end the Calibration] button to return to the service menu. 15. Leave the service menu and return to the main menu of the coffee machine. 16. Test a hot water dispense and check if the amount is the same as specified in the hot water recipe.

menu.title: Recipe settings (Filterfresh Medium)
menu.text: Water/ingredient settings All available recipes are shown in the water/ingredient settings menu. The water and ingredient dosage and other recipe settings can be adjusted. By selecting a beverage you can adjust the recipe. More information about this is given in the next chapter. Strength control % In ‘strength control %’ you can adjust the maximum strength variation (in %) for ‘Main product strength’ (for example coffee), and for ‘milk’ and ‘sugar’. This lets a user set the preferred strength for a consumption. Milk/sugar available The milk or sugar option can be switched off. If switched off, the milk/sugar selection is not shown in the detailed selection menu. Selection available Recipes can be selected by users in the main menu when ‘Y’ (Yes) is selected in the ‘Selection available’ menu. If ‘N’ (No) is selected, the consumption type is not shown in the main menu. Number selection available If the selection is set to ‘Not available’, the number selection button is not shown in the main menu. Tap the button to toggle the selection between ‘Available’ and ‘Not available’.
notes: We recommend making a backup first. See the section 'Backup configuration' in the chapter software configurations.
Strength settings for main products in relation to a brewer must not exceed the value of 10.

menu.title: Uni-brewer example coffee recipe
menu.text: RECIPE EXAMPLE: (Coffee beans) Ingredients for a recipe with coffee beans Beans 1 [or 2] Sub milk Sub sugar Coffee delay Water amount / Water brewer Beans 1 [or 2] Shows the current grinding duration (seconds). This value can be adjusted. If more than one canister is available, select ‘Yes’ for the desired bean ingredient. By selecting ‘test’ you can test the current output quantity of ground coffee. Sub milk Shows the current duration of the topping feed as well as the duration of the water feed (seconds). These values can be adjusted. Shows the current mixing speed. This value can be adjusted. A higher mixing speed gives more foam. Sub sugar Shows the current delay and duration of the sugar feed as well as the duration of the water feed. These values can be adjusted. Coffee delay Shows the current grinding delay (seconds), this value can be adjusted. Water amount (ml) Shows the minimum water volume that passes through during your recipe. This value can be adjusted. Total water amount (ml) Shows the current mixing speed. This value can be adjusted. The final cup volume is the volume of the coffee water + the volume(s) of the sub ingredients. Test Test the recipe.
notes: Which options are available depends on the model/configuration and the login credentials.
Do not adjust the grinding speed (the default value is 100).
Make sure the coffee delay value is higher than the grinding duration value set for beans 1 and beans 2.

If the product appears more than once in the menu, the product is added in several steps. Select ‘product’ to adjust the duration of each step. The delay between the steps is specified in the ‘Coffee delay’ field.
Each sub ingredient has a specified water volume value. This value is included in the total water value.

menu.title: Software configurations (Filterfresh Medium / Filterfresh Small)
menu.text: Select active configuration: choose the configuration file the machine should work with. The configuration file that is active now is grey. All other, inactive files are green. Delete active configuration: deletes a configuration file. Back up configuration: a copy is made of the active configuration with all its settings. You will find this saved file in the menu “Select active configuration”. The backup file name is the original name with a date stamp added (year, month, day and time). Example: Original file name: <MODEL><VERSION>.mvq <MODEL> = name and model of the machine <VERSION> = software version Backup file name: <MODEL><VERSION>_YYMMDDTIME.mvq Load configuration from USB YY = year (20 = 2020) MM = month (01 = January) DD = day (04 = 4th day of the month) TIME = time (1430 = 14:30) Default device 0 is available (only if a USB stick is inserted). You can browse the folders on the stick to find the configuration file you need. The file loaded from the stick is automatically selected as the active configuration. Save configuration to USB: this saves the currently active file onto the USB stick.

menu.title: Cup sensor
menu.text: Show signal: the signal of both sensors can be read individually. That way the visibility of a cup can also be tested. Cup sensor setting: the sensitivity of the cup sensor is adjustable. The value can be set between 0 and 4,000. The value 0 means switched off. The machine then works essentially without a sensor. A higher value means less sensitive. So to detect a transparent or dark cup the value has to be set low. The default is 100. That is the optimal value and gives the best detection for most cups. If the machine has two cup sensors, both can be set individually. Sensor 1 = middle sensor. Sensor 2 = right-hand sensor, hot (and cold -- optional) water.
notes: Black or transparent cups cannot be detected. We advise switching the sensors off if black or transparent cups are used.

menu.title: Boiler temperature
menu.text: Temperature settings Temperature setting gives the possibility to change the desired boiler temperature. Show boiler temperature Recommended boiler temperature settings: Boiler Temperature Boiler 1 (pressure) 92 °C Boiler 2 (open) 91 °C Show boiler temperature will show the actual temperature of the boilers in degrees Celcius. The optimal temperature setting of the pressure boiler is 92 ºC. If no consumptions are made, the temperature in the boiler will automatically rise by 6 ºC in about 25 minutes. The first consumption with a cold brewer is now brewed with incoming water on a higher temperature, compensating the colder brewer.

menu.title: Payment settings
menu.text: Via the payment settings menu the product prices and the functions of the payment system can be set. Consumption prices For setting the prices for all available consumptions. For each individual consumption type 2 price lists are available: price list 1 and price list 2. Free/paid vend Set the machine to free vend or paid mode. View active price lists Activate the required price list. Multi vend A payment system can run in multi vend or single vend. Multi vend means you can select more than 1 consumption after each other. You get your change or your card back after pressing the return button on the change giver or card reader. Single vend means you get your change or your card back directly after the consumption has been dispensed. Overpay allowed • ‘Overpay allowed’ means it is possible to insert more money than the highest consumption price. • ‘Exact payment’ means it is not possible to insert more money than the highest consumption price. MDB coin settings The coin settings can be changed in the software if they are set in the loaded configuration file. MDB bill settings The bill settings can be changed in the software if they are set in the loaded configuration file.

During the warming-up period a message is shown. If the machine is not used for an hour, the Eco mode is activated. View active price lists Multi vend Activate the required price list. A payment system can run in multi vend or single vend. Multi vend means you can select more than 1 consumption after each other. You get your change or your card back after pressing the return button on the change giver or card reader. Single vend means you get your change or your card back directly after the consumption has been dispensed. Overpay allowed • ‘Overpay allowed’ means it is possible to insert more money than the highest consumption price. • ‘Exact payment’ means it is not possible to insert more money than the highest consumption price. MDB coin settings The coin settings can be changed in the software if they are set in the loaded configuration file. MDB bill settings The bill settings can be changed in the software if they are set in the loaded configuration file.

menu.title: Canister settings
menu.text: The coffee machine can show a message when the canisters are almost empty. If the coffee machine knows the starting weight of the ingredient in the canister and the amount dispensed with every recipe, the machine calculates the available amount after every dispense and shows a message when the preset levels are reached. Enable/Disable The level detection message can be enabled/disabled for each canister. 1. Tap [Ingredient] for the ingredient canister that has to be switched on/off. 2. The [Canister level detection enabled] button shows the current setting. 3. Tap [On/Off] and the [button] to change the setting. Calibrating Perform the following steps: 1. Fill the ingredient canisters as usual. 2. Weigh the completely filled canister. 3. Tap the correct [Ingredient] button. 4. Tap [Canister net weight] and enter the weight (in grams). 5. Tap [Canister level message] and enter the percentage (fill level) at which the message Canister almost empty has to be shown. 6. Tap [Calibrate product motor]. 7. Follow the steps on the screen and the explanation below. 8. Hold the cup under the canister outlet and tap [Start]. ▪The product motor runs for 3 seconds (only to fill the outlet). ▪Empty the cup. ▪The second screen is shown. 9. Hold the empty cup under the canister outlet and tap [Start] again. ▪The product motor runs for 10 seconds. ▪The last calibration screen is shown. 10. Weigh the amount of ingredient in the cup. 11. Tap [Quantity] on the screen and enter the weight of the cup with ingredients. 12. The calibration is now complete. 13. If needed, tap [Canister level detection enabled] to activate the settings.

menu.title: Error settings
menu.text: This menu contains information and settings (depending on model, configuration type and login level) for the available warnings and errors. Warning = message on the screen only. Error = message on the screen, machine (partly) out of operation. Change error conditions With this function the condition at which a warning or error occurs can be adjusted. Possible settings: • Waste bin warning (coffee residue / total grinder running time) Indicates the number of cycles before the message “Waste bin full” is shown on the screen. • Waste bin error (coffee residue / total grinder running time) Indicates the number of cycles before the message “Empty waste bin” is shown on the screen. When this message appears, all coffee selections are switched off. • Brewer cleaning warning (time in seconds) (*) Indicates the time before the message “Rinse brewer with tablet” is shown on the screen. The time is given in seconds. • Brewer cleaning error (time in seconds) (*) Indicates the time before the message “Rinse brewer with tablet!!” is shown on the screen. The time is given in seconds. When this message appears, all coffee selections are blocked. • Water filter warning (consumptions) (**) This counter only counts the hot consumptions and cleaning cycles. Indicates the number of consumptions that pass through the water filter before the message “Replace water filter” appears on the screen. • Water filter error (consumptions) (**) Indicates the number of consumptions that pass through the water filter before the message “Replace water filter” appears on the screen. With the message “Replace water filter(!)” the machine keeps working normally. • Clean screen (consumptions) Indicates the number of consumptions before the message "Press HERE to start cleaning. Screen switches off for cleaning" is shown. *) Depending on the software version, these settings are shown here or on the screen Main menu -> Error settings -> Edit cleaning settings. **) Depending on the software version, these settings are shown here or on the screen Main menu -> Water filter settings. Read error counters In this menu various counters can be read. Switch off errors In this menu warnings and errors can be switched on and off. View / reset cleaning settings In this menu the values of the cleaning counters can be viewed or reset (level 4 only). Edit cleaning settings In this menu the following counters can be changed: • Brewer cleaning - counts the time and shows the message “Clean the brewer with a tablet”. This counter is reset during the brewer cleaning procedure. Default: warning interval: 7 days, error interval: 9 days. • Rinsing - shows the message “Daily cleaning required”. This counter is reset during the daily cleaning procedure. Default: warning interval: 24 hours, error interval: 36 hours. • Daily cleaning of the milk system - shows the message “Clean the milk system”. This counter is reset during the daily milk system cleaning procedure. Default: warning interval: 24 hours, error interval: 36 hours. Tap a button to edit a cleaning setting. The following setting options are shown: • Enable [default: Yes] - Tap the button to switch this message counter on or off. • Warning interval (hours) - when the timer reaches this value, the cleaning message is shown as a warning. ▪All selections remain available. • Alternative: Warning days - time entered here in days is converted to the warning interval (hours). • Error interval (hours) - when the timer reaches this value, the cleaning message is shown as an error. ▪Brewer cleaning: all coffee selections are switched off. ▪Rinsing: all selections are switched off. The window “Place a cup and press here” is shown and forces a daily cleaning. ▪Fresh milk: all selections with fresh milk are switched off. • Alternative: Critical days - time entered here in days is converted to an error interval (hours). Reset cleaning error After this button is pressed, the machine beeps and the brewer cleaning message disappears from the screen.

Daily cleaning milk system - shows the message "Clean the Milk system". The daily cleaning milk system procedure resets this counter. Default: Warning time: 24 hours, Error time: 36 hours. Tap a button to edit a cleaning setting. The following setting options are displayed:
Enable [default: Yes] - Tap the button to enable or disable this message counter.
Warning time (hours) - when the timer reaches this value, the cleaning message is displayed as a warning.
All selections can still be used.
Alternative: Warning days - time in days entered here will be recalculated to warning time (hours).
Error time (hours) - when the timer reaches this value, the cleaning message is displayed as an error.
Brewer cleaning: all coffee selections are disabled.
Rinse: all selections are disabled. The window "Place a cup and press here" is displayed and forces a daily rinse.
Fresh Milk: all fresh milk selections are disabled.

Alternative: Critical days - time in days entered here will be recalculated to error time (hours). Reset cleaning error After pressing this button, the machine beeps, and the brewer cleaning message is cleared from the screen.
notes: If the waste is guided to a big waste bin under the machine, both the waste bucket warning and waste bucket error need to be set to “not available”.
The timer will start running after the first dispense containing Fresh Milk.
Be sure the brewer is clean, and no cleaning agent or cleaning powder is left in the brewer.

menu.title: Fan turn-off delay
menu.text: The fan runs for the set time after the last dispense. The time is in minutes. Set to 0 the fan stops as soon as the dispense is finished. Set to 99 the fan keeps running.

menu.title: Fan turn off delay (CEC)
menu.text: The fan will run the set time after the last consumption. Time is set in minutes. If the time is set to 0, the fan stops immediately after the consumption is finished. If the time is set to 99, the fan will run continuously.
steps: Waste bin warning (coffee residue / total grinder running time) Indicates the number of cycles before the message “Waste bin full” is shown on the screen.

Waste bin error (coffee residue / total grinder running time) Indicates the number of cycles before the message “Empty waste bin” is shown on the screen. When this message appears, all coffee selections are switched off.
Brewer cleaning warning (time in seconds) (*) Indicates the time before the message “Rinse brewer with tablet” is shown on the screen. The time is given in seconds.

Brewer cleaning error (time in seconds) (*) Indicates the time before the message “Rinse brewer with tablet!!” is shown on the screen. The time is given in seconds. When this message appears, all coffee selections are blocked.

Water filter warning (consumptions) (**) This counter only counts the hot consumptions and cleaning cycles. Indicates the number of consumptions that pass through the water filter before the message “Replace water filter” appears on the screen.

Water filter error (consumptions) (**) Indicates the number of consumptions that pass through the water filter before the message “Replace water filter” appears on the screen. With the message “Replace water filter(!)” the machine keeps working normally.

Clean screen (consumptions) Indicates the number of consumptions before the message "Press HERE to start cleaning. Screen switches off for cleaning" is shown. *) Depending on the software version, these settings are shown here or on the screen Main menu -> Error settings -> Edit cleaning settings. **) Depending on the software version, these settings are shown here or on the screen Main menu -> Water filter settings. Read error counters In this menu various counters can be read. Switch off errors In this menu warnings and errors can be switched on and off. View / reset cleaning settings In this menu the values of the cleaning counters can be viewed or reset (level 4 only). Edit cleaning settings In this menu the following counters can be changed:

Brewer cleaning - counts the time and shows the message “Clean the brewer with a tablet”. This counter is reset during the brewer cleaning procedure. Default: warning interval: 7 days, error interval: 9 days.
Rinsing - shows the message “Daily cleaning required”. This counter is reset during the daily cleaning procedure. Default: warning interval: 24 hours, error interval: 36 hours.

Daily cleaning of the milk system - shows the message “Clean the milk system”. This counter is reset during the daily milk system cleaning procedure. Default: warning interval: 24 hours, error interval: 36 hours. Tap a button to edit a cleaning setting. The following setting options are shown:
Enable [default: Yes] - Tap the button to switch this message counter on or off.
Warning interval (hours) - when the timer reaches this value, the cleaning message is shown as a warning.
All selections remain available.
Alternative: Warning days - time entered here in days is converted to the warning interval (hours).
Error interval (hours) - when the timer reaches this value, the cleaning message is shown as an error.
Brewer cleaning: all coffee selections are switched off.
Rinsing: all selections are switched off. The window “Place a cup and press here” is shown and forces a daily cleaning.
Fresh milk: all selections with fresh milk are switched off.

Alternative: Critical days - time entered here in days is converted to an error interval (hours). Reset cleaning error After this button is pressed, the machine beeps and the brewer cleaning message disappears from the screen.
notes: If the waste is guided into a large waste bin under the machine, both the waste bin warning and the waste bin error must be set to “not available”.
The timer starts after the first dispense with fresh milk.
Make sure the brewer is clean and that no cleaning agent or cleaning powder is left in the brewer.

menu.title: Change PIN
menu.text: A PIN code can be set in this menu. Once set, the code has to be entered before every dispense. If the machine is in payment mode and a PIN code is set, the drink is dispensed free of charge after the code is entered.

menu.title: Change PIN (CEC)
menu.text: In this menu it is possible to set a PIN code. After setting a PIN code the machine will request entering the code for each consumption. In payment mode when a PIN code is set, the machine will allow a free consumption after entering the PIN code.

menu.title: Change menu (Level 4)
menu.text: Various menu texts (buttons) on the screen can be changed. If the text is part of the recipe, the text, screen position and default cup size (optional) of the recipe can be changed. Example 1 – change text: Tap [Main menu]. All menu texts are shown. Use the [PgDwn] button and tap the recipe button [Coffee beans]. The text in the coffee beans recipe is shown. Tap the [text] button you want to change. Change the text and tap [Save]. Example 2 – change position: In the same recipe tap the current [position] button. Enter the position number you want and tap [Save]. If the position is already taken by another recipe, you can swap the positions of the two recipes. Tap [swap ‘x’ and ‘y’]. Example 3 – change the default cup size: In the same recipe tap the current [cup size] and tap the size you want.
notes: The first entry in a group of recipes is the menu itself.
This only works if cup sizes can be chosen for the recipe.

menu.title: Change menu (Level 4)
menu.text: Various menu (button) texts on the screens can be changed. If the text is part of a recipe, the text, screen location and default cup size (optional) of the recipe can be changed. Example 1 - change text: Tap the [Mainmenu] button. All texts displayed on the menu are shown. Use the [PgDwn] button and locate and tap the [Coffee beans] recipe button. Text in the Coffee beans recipe is displayed. Tap the [text] button that needs to be changed. Change the text and tap the [Save] button. Example 2 - change position: In the same recipe, tap the current [position] button. Enter the desired position number and tap the [Save] button. If the new position already contains a recipe, the positions of the two recipes can be swapped, tap the [Swap 'x' and 'y'] to confirm. Example 3 - change the default cup size: In the same recipe, tap the current [cup size] button and tap the desired cup size.
notes: The first entry in a group of recipes is the menu itself.
This only works if the recipe contains the selectable cup sizes.

menu.title: Empty open boiler
menu.text: If the machine has to be stored for a longer time or transported (cold weather, aircraft), the internal hoses and boilers have to be emptied. The boilers empty by gravity. Procedure: 1. Pull the plug out of the socket. 2. Remove the backplate of the machine. 3. Find the grey hose with plug and clamp at the back of the machine. 4. Pull the plug out of the end of the hose. ▪Hold the end of the hose in a waste bucket or pail (>5 L). 5. Carefully release the hose clamp. ▪Hot water may come out of the boiler. ▪Wait until the boiler is empty. 6. Release the hose clamp and put the plug into the hose.
steps: Pull the plug out of the socket.

Find the grey hose with plug and clamp at the back of the machine.
Pull the plug out of the end of the hose. ▪Hold the end of the hose in a waste bucket or pail (>5 L).
Carefully release the hose clamp. ▪Hot water may come out of the boiler.
Wait until the boiler is empty.

notes: Take care, hot water may come out of the boilers.

menu.title: Empty pressure boilers
menu.text: In case the machine needs to be stored for a longer time, or needs to be transported (freezing weather, plane) the internal hoses and boilers need to be emptied. The boilers are emptied due to gravity. Procedure Perform the following steps: 1. Remove the power cord from the wall socket. 2. Remove the back cover plate from the machine. 3. Remove the plug from the metal elbow or T coupling right after the pump(s). See inset. 4. Connect a 6 mm hose to the elbow. ▪ Make sure the outlet of this hose is lower than the inlet valve of the machine. 5. Put the power cord back in the wall socket. 6. Enter the service menu and select: Empty boiler. ▪ The pumps will run for a short time, the 3-way valve opens to add air to the system. Slowly all water runs out of the boiler and hoses.

Locate the grey hose with plug and the cut off clamp at the back of the machine. 4. Remove the plug at the end of the hose. ▪ Hold the end of the hose in a bucket or container (>5L). 5. Loosen the hose cut off clamp carefully. ▪ Potentially hot water will be drained out of the boiler. ▪ Wait until the boiler is empty. 6. Release the hose cut off clamp and place the plug in the hose.

menu.title: Display settings (Level 4) — CoEx Medium
menu.text: In display settings, you can invert the backlight. The user menu screen will turn black in case this setting is incorrect. The service menu is always available though. Select “Invert backlight” to solve a blacked out user menu.

menu.title: Audio settings (CoEx XL Medium)
menu.text: In this menu tab the multimedia volume can be adjusted. Volume standby (video) Adjust the multimedia volume in standby mode. Volume dispensing (video) Adjust the multimedia volume during dispensing.

menu.title: Edit active language items (Level 4)
menu.text: Change the screen texts for optional ingredients and other texts. 1. Tap [edit] beside the text you want to change. 2. Change the text and tap [Save]. Example: tap [Rolling advertisement text]. The current text is shown. Tap the green button on the right. Enter the text you want and tap [Save]. The changed advertisement text appears on the main screen.

menu.title: Display settings (Level 4) — CoEx Small / CoEx XL Small
menu.text: Display settings let you invert the backlight. The user menu turns black if this setting is wrong. The service menu does stay available. Select ‘Invert backlight’ to undo a blacked-out user menu.

menu.title: Component available (Level 4)
menu.text: This section lets you switch hardware parts in the coffee machine on and off. Recipes (or parts of them) that use a switched-off part are disabled. Other recipes (parts) can still be used. Example: Chocolate, tap [Available] and then [No]. The ingredient is now switched off and every recipe in the menus with chocolate as an ingredient is suppressed.

menu.text: Display settings let you invert the backlight. The user menu turns black if this setting is wrong. The service menu does stay available. Select ‘Invert backlight’ to undo a blacked-out user menu.

menu.title: Edit active language items (Level 4) — CoEx Small
menu.text: Change the screen texts for optional ingredients and other texts. 1. Tap [edit] beside the text you want to change. 2. Change the text and tap [Save]. Example: tap [Rolling advertisement text]. The current text is shown. Tap the green button on the right. Enter the text you want and tap [Save]. The changed advertisement text appears on the main screen.

The changed advert text is visible on the main screen.

menu.title: Service position CoEx XL (CoEx XL Small)
menu.text: The brewer can be put into the service position. Use this function for maintenance, for replacing parts or to clear a brewer blockage. See the chapter Putting the brewer in the service position for more information.

menu.title: Counters
menu.text: The counters section shows the different counters in the coffee machine. • Recipe counters: show the number of free and paid drinks dispensed. • User counters: show the total running time of the grinder, use of a PIN code, resets of the waste bucket and the number of clean-screen messages. • Component counters: show the running time of the hardware components. • Cleaning counters: show the time elapsed since the last cleaning message.
steps: Recipe counters: show the number of free and paid drinks dispensed.
User counters: show the total running time of the grinder, use of a PIN code, resets of the waste bucket and the number of clean-screen messages.
Component counters: show the running time of the hardware components.
Cleaning counters: show the time elapsed since the last cleaning message.

menu.title: Component available (Level 4) — CoEx Small
menu.text: This section lets you switch hardware parts in the coffee machine on and off. Recipes (or parts of them) that use a switched-off part are disabled. Other recipes (parts) can still be used. Example: Chocolate, tap [Available] and then [No]. The ingredient is now switched off and every recipe in the menus with chocolate as an ingredient is suppressed.

menu.title: Reset hardware counters (Level 4)
menu.text: The counters described in the previous chapter can be reset. Only use this function when the technical support department asks you to.

menu.text: In this section it is possible to disable and enable hardware parts in the coffee machine. The code will guide the user to a web page with a selection of the drinks available on that specific machine. After placing a cup and selection of the desired drink on the smartphone, the machine will prepare the drink as usual. The screen shows if the Touchless Interface is enabled or not. Tap the [Yes] or [No] button to determine if the QR code is displayed in the main menu. To store a printable image of the QR code (for that specific machine) on a USB stick, first insert a stick in the USB port and then tap the [Save] button.
